words.en: Pumas are large, cat-like animals which are found in America.
words.zh: 美洲狮是一种体形似猫的大型动物，产于美洲。

words.en: When reports came into London Zoo that a wild puma had been spotted forty-five miles south of London, they were not taken seriously.
words.zh: 当伦敦动物园收到有关在伦敦以南四十五英里处发现一只野生美洲狮的报道时，他们并没有认真对待。

words.en: However, as the evidence began to accumulate, experts from the Zoo felt obliged to investigate, for the descriptions given by people who claimed to have seen the puma were extraordinarily similar.
words.zh: 然而，随着证据开始积累，动物园的专家们觉得有必要进行调查，因为那些声称见过美洲狮的人所给出的描述非常相似。

words.en: The hunt for the puma began in a small village where a woman picking blackberries saw 'a large cat'only five yards away from her.
words.zh: 猎杀美洲狮的行动始于一个小村庄，一名采摘黑莓的妇女看到“一只大猫”距离她仅五码远。

words.en: It immediately ran away when she saw it, and experts confirmed that a puma will not attack a human being unless it is cornered.
words.zh: 它一看到它就立即逃跑，专家证实美洲狮不会攻击人类，除非它被逼入绝境。

words.en: The search proved difficult, for the puma was often observed at one place in the morning and at another place twenty miles away in the evening.
words.zh: 搜索被证明是困难的，因为人们经常在早上在一个地方观察到美洲狮，晚上在二十英里外的另一个地方观察到美洲狮。

words.en: Wherever it went, it left behind it a trail of dead deer and small animals like rabbits.
words.zh: 它所到之处，都留下了死鹿和兔子等小动物的踪迹。

words.en: Paw prints were seen in a number of places and puma fur was found clinging to bushes.
words.zh: 在许多地方都可以看到爪子印记，灌木丛上还发现了美洲狮的皮毛。

words.en: Several people complained of 'cat-like noises' at night and a businessman on a fishing trip saw the puma up a tree.
words.zh: 有几个人抱怨晚上听到“猫一样的噪音”，一名商人在钓鱼时看到美洲狮在树上。

words.en: The experts were now fully convinced that the animal was a puma, but where had it come from?
words.zh: 专家们现在完全确信这只动物是美洲狮，但它是从哪里来的呢？

words.en: As no pumas had been reported missing from any zoo in the country, this one must have been in the possession of a private collector and somehow managed to escape.
words.zh: 由于该国任何动物园都没有美洲狮失踪的报道，因此这只美洲狮一定是由一位私人收藏家拥有并以某种方式逃脱的。

words.en: The hunt went on for several weeks, but the puma was not caught.
words.zh: 狩猎持续了几个星期，但美洲狮没有被抓到。

words.en: It is disturbing to think that a dangerous wild animal is still at large in the quiet countryside.
words.zh: 一想到危险的野生动物仍然在安静的乡村逍遥法外，就令人不安。

words.en: Our vicar is always raising money for one cause or another, but he has never managed to get enough money to have the church clock repaired.
words.zh: 我们的牧师总是为了这样或那样的原因筹集资金，但他从来没有筹到足够的钱来修理教堂的钟。

words.en: The big clock which used to strike the hours day and night was damaged many years ago and has been silent ever since.
words.zh: 这座曾经日夜报时的大钟在很多年前就被损坏了，从此就沉寂了。

words.en: One night, however, our vicar woke up with a start: the clock was striking the hours!
words.zh: 然而一天晚上，我们的牧师惊醒了：时钟已经敲响了！

words.en: Looking at his watch, he saw that it was one o'clock, but the bell struck thirteen times before it stopped.
words.zh: 看看表，已经一点了，钟声却敲了十三下才停。

words.en: Armed with a torch, the vicar went up into the clock tower to see what was going on.
words.zh: 牧师手持火把，走进钟楼查看发生了什么事。

words.en: In the torchlight, he caught sight of a figure whom he immediately recognized as Bill Wilkins, our local grocer.
words.zh: 在手电筒的灯光下，他看到了一个人影，他立即认出他是比尔·威尔金斯，我们当地的杂货店老板。

words.en: 'Whatever are you doing up here Bill?' asked the vicar in surprise.
words.zh: “比尔，你在这儿做什么？”牧师惊讶地问道。

words.en: 'I'm trying to repair the bell, ' answered Bill.
words.zh: “我正在尝试修理门铃，”比尔回答道。

words.en: 'I've been coming up here night after night for weeks now.
words.zh: “几周来我一直夜复一夜地来到这里。

words.en: You see, I was hoping to give you a surprise.'
words.zh: 你看，我本来希望给你一个惊喜。”

words.en: 'You certainly did give me a surprise!' said the vicar.
words.zh: “你确实给了我一个惊喜！”牧师说。

words.en: 'You've probably woken up everyone in the village as well.
words.zh: “你可能也吵醒了村子里的每个人。

words.en: Still, I'm glad the bell is working again.'
words.zh: 尽管如此，我还是很高兴铃声又响了。

words.en: 'That's the trouble, vicar, 'answered Bill.
words.zh: “这就是问题所在，牧师，”比尔回答道。

words.en: 'It's working all right, but I'm afraid that at one o'clock it will strike thirteen times and there's nothing I can do about it.'
words.zh: “它工作得很好，但我担心一点钟它会敲响十三次，我对此无能为力。”

words.en: 'We'll get used to that, Bill, 'said the vicar.
words.zh: “我们会习惯的，比尔，”牧师说。

words.en: 'Thirteen is not as good as one, but it's better than nothing.
words.zh: 十三虽不如一，但也比没有好。

words.en: Now let's go downstairs and have a cup of tea.'
words.zh: 现在我们下楼去喝杯茶吧。”

words.en: Some time ago, an interesting discovery was made by archaeologists on the Aegean island of Kea.
words.zh: 前段时间，考古学家在爱琴海的基亚岛上有了一个有趣的发现。

words.en: An American team explored a temple which stands in an ancient city on the promontory of Ayia Irini.
words.zh: 一支美国团队探索了位于阿伊亚伊里尼海角一座古城中的一座寺庙。

words.en: The city at one time must have been prosperous, for it enjoyed a high level of civilization.
words.zh: 这座城市曾经一定很繁荣，因为它享有很高的文明水平。

words.en: Houses — often three storeys high — were built of stone.
words.zh: 房屋通常是三层高，是用石头建造的。

words.en: They had large rooms with beautifully decorated walls.
words.zh: 他们的房间很大，墙壁装饰得很漂亮。

words.en: The city was even equipped with a drainage system, for a great many clay pipes were found beneath the narrow streets.
words.zh: 这座城市甚至配备了排水系统，因为在狭窄的街道下发现了大量粘土管道。

words.en: The temple which the archaeologists explored was used as a place of worship from the fifteenth century B.C. until Roman times.
words.zh: 考古学家探索的这座寺庙从公元前十五世纪起就被用作礼拜场所。直到罗马时代。

words.en: In the most sacred room of the temple, clay fragments of fifteen statues were found.
words.zh: 在寺庙最神圣的房间里，发现了十五尊雕像的粘土碎片。

words.en: Each of these represented a goddess and had, at one time, been painted.
words.zh: 每一幅都代表一位女神，并且曾经被绘制过。

words.en: The body of one statue was found among remains dating from the 15th century B.C. Its missing head happened to be among remains of the fifth century B.C. This head must have been found in Classical times and carefully preserved.
words.zh: 在公元前 15 世纪的遗迹中发现了一尊雕像的尸体。它失踪的头恰好是公元前五世纪的遗骸之一。这颗头像一定是在古典时期发现的，并且被精心保存。

words.en: It was very old and precious even then.
words.zh: 即使在当时，它也非常古老和珍贵。

words.en: When the archaeologists reconstructed the fragments, they were amazed to find that the goddess turned out to be a very modern-looking woman.
words.zh: 当考古学家重建这些碎片时，他们惊讶地发现女神竟然是一位长相非常现代的女性。

words.en: She stood three feet high and her hands rested on her hips.
words.zh: 她站得三英尺高，双手放在臀部。

words.en: She was wearing a full-length skirt which swept the ground.
words.zh: 她穿着一条拖地的长裙。

words.en: Despite her great age, she was very graceful indeed, but, so far, the archaeologists have been unable to discover her identity.
words.zh: 尽管她年事已高，但她确实非常优雅，但到目前为止，考古学家还无法发现她的身份。

courses.title: Lesson 4 · The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs

words.en: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
words.zh: 如今，从事体力工作的人通常比在办公室工作的人赚更多的钱。

words.en: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as 'white-collar workers' for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
words.zh: 在办公室工作的人经常被称为“白领工人”，原因很简单，因为他们通常穿着有领子、打着领带去上班。

words.en: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
words.zh: 这就是人性，很多人往往愿意牺牲更高的工资来换取成为白领工人的特权。

words.en: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation.
words.zh: 这可能会引起奇怪的情况，就像在埃尔斯米尔公司担任清洁工的阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯的例子一样。

words.en: When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
words.zh: 结婚后，阿尔夫不好意思向妻子谈论他的工作。

words.en: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.
words.zh: 他只是告诉她他在公司工作。

words.en: Every morning, he left home dressed in a smart black suit.
words.zh: 每天早上，他都会穿着一身漂亮的黑色西装离开家。

words.en: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
words.zh: 然后他换上工作服，在接下来的八个小时里担任清洁工。

words.en: Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit.
words.zh: 晚上回家之前，他洗了个澡，换回了西装。

words.en: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret.
words.zh: 阿尔夫这样做了两年多，他的清洁工同事保守了他的秘密。

words.en: Alf's wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job.
words.zh: 阿尔夫的妻子从未发现她嫁给了一名清洁工，而且也永远不会发现，因为阿尔夫刚刚找到了另一份工作。

words.en: He will soon be working in an office.
words.zh: 他很快就会在办公室工作。

words.en: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
words.zh: 他的收入将只有以前的一半，但他觉得自己地位的提高是值得的。

words.en: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him 'Mr. Bloggs', not 'Alf'.
words.zh: 从此以后，他整天穿着西装，别人都叫他“先生”。博客”，而不是“阿尔夫”。

words.en: Editors of newspapers and magazines often go to extremes to provide their readers with unimportant facts and statistics.
words.zh: 报纸和杂志的编辑经常走极端，向读者提供不重要的事实和统计数据。

words.en: Last year a journalist had been instructed by a well-known magazine to write an article on the president's palace in a new African republic.
words.zh: 去年，一名记者受一家知名杂志的委托，撰写一篇有关非洲新共和国总统府的文章。

words.en: When the article arrived, the editor read the first sentence and then refused to publish it.
words.zh: 文章到达后，编辑看了第一句话，然后拒绝发表。

words.en: The article began:'Hundreds of steps lead to the high wall which surrounds the president's palace.'
words.zh: 文章开头这样写道：“数百级台阶通向总统府周围的高墙。”

words.en: The editor at once sent the journalist a fax instructing him to find out the exact number of steps and the height of the wall.
words.zh: 编辑立即给记者发了一份传真，让他查清楚具体的台阶数和墙的高度。

words.en: The journalist immediately set out to obtain these important facts, but he took a long time to send them.
words.zh: 记者立即着手获取这些重要事实，但花了很长时间才发送出去。

words.en: Meanwhile, the editor was getting impatient, for the magazine would soon go to press.
words.zh: 与此同时，编辑也变得不耐烦了，因为杂志很快就要付印了。

words.en: He sent the journalist two more faxes, but received no reply.
words.zh: 他又给记者发了两份传真，但没有收到回复。

words.en: He sent yet another fax informing the journalist that if he did not reply soon he would be fired.
words.zh: 他又发了另一份传真，通知记者如果不尽快回复，他将被解雇。

words.en: When the journalist again failed to reply, the editor reluctantly published the article as it had originally been written.
words.zh: 当记者再次没有回复时，编辑无奈地按原样发表了这篇文章。

words.en: A week later, the editor at last received a fax from the journalist.
words.zh: 一周后，编辑终于收到了记者发来的传真。

words.en: Not only had the poor man been arrested, but he had been sent to prison as well.
words.zh: 这个可怜的人不仅被捕了，还被送进了监狱。

words.en: However, he had at last been allowed to send a fax in which he informed the editor that he had been arrested while counting the 1,084 steps leading to the 15th foot wall which surrounded the president's palace.
words.zh: 然而，他最终被允许发送一份传真，其中他告诉编辑，他在数通向总统府周围第 15 英尺墙的 1,084 级台阶时被捕。

words.en: The expensive shops in a famous arcade near Piccadilly were just opening.
words.zh: 皮卡迪利附近著名的拱廊内的昂贵商店刚刚开业。

words.en: At this time of the morning, the arcade was almost empty.
words.zh: 早上这个时候，拱廊里几乎空无一人。

words.en: Mr. Taylor, the owner of a jewellery shop was admiring a new window display.
words.zh: 一家珠宝店的店主泰勒先生正在欣赏新的橱窗展示。

words.en: Two of his assistants had been working busily since 8 o'clock and had only just finished.
words.zh: 他的两个助手从八点就开始忙碌，现在才刚刚结束。

words.en: Diamond necklaces and rings had been beautifully arranged on a background of black velvet.
words.zh: 钻石项链和戒指精美地排列在黑色天鹅绒的背景上。

words.en: After gazing at the display for several minutes, Mr. Taylor went back into his shop.
words.zh: 泰勒先生盯着陈列品看了几分钟后，回到了他的店里。

words.en: The silence was suddenly broken when a large car, with its headlights on and its horn blaring, roared down the arcade.
words.zh: 当一辆大车开着头灯，鸣着喇叭，沿着拱廊呼啸而过时，寂静突然被打破。

words.en: It came to a stop outside the jeweller's.
words.zh: 车子在珠宝店外停了下来。

words.en: One man stayed at the wheel while two others with black stockings over their faces jumped out and smashed the window of the shop with iron bars.
words.zh: 一名男子留在了方向盘上，另外两名脸上蒙着黑丝袜的男子跳了出来，用铁棍砸碎了商店的窗户。

words.en: While this was going on, Mr. Taylor was upstairs.
words.zh: 当这一切发生时，泰勒先生在楼上。

words.en: He and his staff began throwing furniture out of the window.
words.zh: 他和他的员工开始把家具扔出窗外。

words.en: Chairs and tables went flying into the arcade.
words.zh: 椅子和桌子飞进了拱廊。

words.en: One of the thieves was struck by a heavy statue, but he was too busy helping himself to diamonds to notice any pain.
words.zh: 其中一名小偷被一尊沉重的雕像击中，但他正忙着取钻石，没有注意到任何疼痛。

words.en: The raid was all over in three minutes, for the men scrambled back into the car and it moved off at a fantastic speed.
words.zh: 袭击在三分钟内就结束了，人们爬回车上，车以惊人的速度开走了。

words.en: Just as it was leaving, Mr. Taylor rushed out and ran after it throwing ashtrays and vases, but it was impossible to stop the thieves.
words.zh: 正当它要离开时，泰勒先生冲了出来，扔烟灰缸和花瓶追赶它，但无法阻止窃贼。

words.en: They had got away with thousands of pounds worth of diamonds.
words.zh: 他们偷走了价值数千英镑的钻石。

words.en: Has it ever happened to you?
words.zh: 你有过这样的经历吗？

words.en: Have you ever put your trousers in the washing machine and then remembered there was a large bank note in your back pocket?
words.zh: 您是否曾经将裤子放入洗衣机，然后想起后口袋里有一张大钞票？

words.en: When you rescued your trousers, did you find the note was whiter than white?
words.zh: 当你救出你的裤子时，你有没有发现纸条比白色更白？

words.en: People who live in Britain needn't despair when they make mistakes like this (and a lot of people do)!
words.zh: 生活在英国的人们在犯这样的错误时不必绝望（很多人都这样做）！

words.en: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
words.zh: 对他们来说幸运的是，英格兰银行有一个名为 Mutilated Ladies 的团队，负责处理那些将钱喂给机器或狗的人提出的索赔。

words.en: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
words.zh: 看来狗很喜欢嚼钱！

words.en: A recent case concerns Jane Butlin whose fiance, John, runs a successful furniture business.
words.zh: 最近的一个案例涉及简·布特林，她的未婚夫约翰经营着一家成功的家具企业。

words.en: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing ￡3,000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
words.zh: 约翰度过了非常愉快的一天，他将装有 3000 英镑的钱包放入微波炉中妥善保管。

words.en: Then he and Jane went horse-riding.
words.zh: 然后他和简去骑马。

words.en: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiance's wallet as well.
words.zh: 当他们回到家时，简用微波炉煮了晚餐，不知不觉中，她的未婚夫的钱包也被煮熟了。

words.en: Imagine their dismay when they found a beautifully-cooked wallet and notes turned to ash!
words.zh: 想象一下当他们发现一个精美的钱包和纸条变成灰烬时的沮丧！

words.en: John went to see his bank manager who sent the remains of wallet and the money to the special department of the Bank of England in Newcastle: the Mutilated Ladies!
words.zh: 约翰去见了他的银行经理，他将钱包的残骸和钱送到了纽卡斯尔的英格兰银行特别部门：残缺不全的女士们！

words.en: They examined the remains and John got all his money back.
words.zh: 他们检查了遗体，约翰拿回了所有的钱。

words.en: 'So long as there's something to identify, we will give people their money back,' said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
words.zh: 该银行发言人表示，只要有问题可以确认，我们就会退还人们的钱。

words.en: 'Last year, we paid ￡1.5 million on 21,000 claims.'
words.zh: “去年，我们为 21,000 起索赔支付了 150 万英镑。”

words.en: The Great St. Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
words.zh: 大圣伯纳德山口连接瑞士和意大利。

words.en: At 2,473 metres, it is the highest mountain pass in Europe.
words.zh: 海拔 2,473 米，是欧洲最高的山口。

words.en: The famous monastery of St. Bernard, which was founded in the eleventh century, lies about a mile away.
words.zh: 著名的圣伯纳德修道院建于十一世纪，距离酒店约有一英里。

words.en: For hundreds of years, St. Bernard dogs have saved the lives of travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
words.zh: 数百年来，圣伯纳犬拯救了穿越危险山口的旅行者的生命。

words.en: These friendly dogs, which were first brought from Asia, were used as watchdogs even in Roman times.
words.zh: 这些友善的狗最初是从亚洲带来的，即使在罗马时代也被用作看门狗。

words.en: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous, but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
words.zh: 现在，山上修建了一条隧道，山口的危险性降低了，但每年，每当旅行者遇到困难时，这些狗仍然会被送到雪地里。

words.en: Despite the new tunnel, there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
words.zh: 尽管修建了新隧道，仍有少数人贸然尝试步行过关。

words.en: During the summer months, the monastery is very busy, for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
words.zh: 在夏季的几个月里，修道院非常繁忙，因为有成千上万的人乘汽车穿越山口来参观。

words.en: As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
words.zh: 由于周围人太多，狗必须被关在一个特殊的围栏里。

words.en: In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
words.zh: 然而，到了冬天，修道院里的生活就大不相同了。

words.en: The temperature drops to -30 degrees, and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
words.zh: 气温降至-30度，很少有人尝试穿越山口。

words.en: The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
words.zh: 僧侣们更喜欢冬天而不是夏天，因为冬天有更多的隐私。

words.en: The dogs have greater freedom, too, for they are allowed to wander outside their enclosure.
words.zh: 狗也有更大的自由，因为它们可以在围栏外漫步。

words.en: The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
words.zh: 冬季，修道院唯一的常客是圣诞节和复活节期间去那里的滑雪者。

words.en: These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.
words.zh: 这些热爱山间宁静的年轻人在圣伯纳德修道院总是受到热烈的欢迎。

words.en: Cats never fail to fascinate human beings.
words.zh: 猫总是让人类着迷。

words.en: They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well.
words.zh: 他们对人类友善而深情，但他们也过着自己神秘的生活。

words.en: They never become submissive like dogs and horses.
words.zh: 他们永远不会像狗和马那样变得顺从。

words.en: As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence.
words.zh: 结果，人类学会了尊重猫科动物的独立性。

words.en: Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives.
words.zh: 大多数猫一生都对人类持怀疑态度。

words.en: One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives.
words.zh: 关于猫最让我们着迷的事情之一是人们普遍相信它们有九条生命。

words.en: Apparently, there is a good deal of truth in this idea.
words.zh: 显然，这个想法有很多道理。

words.en: A cat's ability to survive falls is based on fact.
words.zh: 猫跌倒后的存活能力是有事实依据的。

words.en: Recently the New York Animal Medical Centre made a study of 132 cats over a period of five months.
words.zh: 最近，纽约动物医学中心对 132 只猫进行了为期 5 个月的研究。

words.en: All these cats had one experience in common: they had fallen off high buildings, yet only eight of them died from shock or injuries.
words.zh: 这些猫都有一个共同的经历：从高楼坠落，但只有八只因惊吓或受伤而死亡。

words.en: Of course, New York is the ideal place for such an interesting study, because there is no shortage of tall buildings.
words.zh: 当然，纽约是进行这种有趣研究的理想场所，因为这里不乏高楼大厦。

words.en: There are plenty of high-rise windowsills to fall from!
words.zh: 有很多高层窗台可以从上面掉下来！

words.en: One cat, Sabrina, fell 32 storeys, yet only suffered from a broken tooth.
words.zh: 一只名叫萨布丽娜（Sabrina）的猫从 32 层楼坠落，但只摔断了一颗牙齿。

words.en: 'Cats behave like well-trained paratroopers,' a doctor said.
words.zh: “猫的行为就像训练有素的伞兵，”一位医生说。

words.en: It seems that the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves.
words.zh: 看来猫摔得越远，它们受伤的可能性就越小。

words.en: In a long drop, they reach speeds of 60 miles an hour and more.
words.zh: 在长距离下降中，它们的速度可达每小时 60 英里甚至更高。

words.en: At high speeds, falling cats have time to relax.
words.zh: 在高速行驶时，坠落的猫有时间放松。

words.en: They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels.
words.zh: 它们像飞鼠一样伸展双腿。

words.en: This increases their air-resistance and reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.
words.zh: 这增加了它们的空气阻力并减少了它们撞击地面时的冲击力。

courses.title: Lesson 10 · The Loss of the Titanic

words.en: The great ship, Titanic sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912.
words.zh: 1912 年 4 月 10 日，泰坦尼克号这艘伟大的船从南安普顿驶往纽约。

words.en: She was carrying 1,316 passengers and a crew of 891.
words.zh: 她载有 1,316 名乘客和 891 名船员。

words.en: Even by modern standards, the 46,000 ton Titanic was a colossal ship.
words.zh: 即使按照现代标准，46,000 吨的泰坦尼克号也是一艘巨大的船舶。

words.en: At that time, however, she was not only the largest ship that had ever been built, but was regarded as unsinkable, for she had sixteen water-tight compartments.
words.zh: 然而，当时她不仅是有史以来建造的最大的船，而且被认为是不沉的，因为她有十六个水密舱室。

words.en: Even if two of these were flooded, she would still be able to float.
words.zh: 即使其中两个被淹没，她仍然能够漂浮。

words.en: The tragic sinking of this great liner will always be remembered, for she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life.
words.zh: 这艘伟大客轮的悲惨沉没将永远被人们铭记，因为她在第一次航行中就沉没了，造成了严重的人员伤亡。

words.en: Four days after setting out, while the Titanic was sailing across the icy waters of the North Atlantic, a huge iceberg was suddenly spotted by a lookout.
words.zh: 出发四天后，当泰坦尼克号航行穿过北大西洋冰冷的水域时，瞭望员突然发现了一座巨大的冰山。

words.en: After the alarm had been given, the great ship turned sharply to avoid a direct collision.
words.zh: 警报发出后，大船急转方向，避免了直接相撞。

words.en: The Titanic turned just in time, narrowly missing the immense wall of ice which rose over 100 feet out of the water beside her.
words.zh: 泰坦尼克号及时转弯，险些撞上了她旁边那面高出水面 100 多英尺的巨大冰墙。

words.en: Suddenly, there was a slight trembling sound from below, and the captain went down to see what had happened.
words.zh: 突然，下面传来轻微的颤抖声，队长下去查看发生了什么事。

words.en: The noise had been so faint that no one thought that the ship had been damaged.
words.zh: 噪音非常微弱，没有人认为这艘船已经受损。

words.en: Below, the captain realized to his horror that the Titanic was sinking rapidly, for five of her sixteen watertight compartments had already been flooded!
words.zh: 下面，船长惊恐地发现泰坦尼克号正在迅速下沉，因为她的十六个水密舱室中的五个已经被淹没了！

words.en: The order to abandon ship was given and hundreds of people plunged into the icy water.
words.zh: 弃船命令下达，数百人跳入冰冷的水中。

words.en: As there were not enough life-boats for everybody, 1,500 lives were lost.
words.zh: 由于没有足够的救生艇供所有人使用，1,500 人丧生。

words.en: Customs Officers are quite tolerant these days, but they can still stop you when you are going through the Green Channel and have nothing to declare.
words.zh: 现在海关官员已经很宽容了，但是当你通过绿色通道并且没有任何东西需要申报时，他们仍然可以阻止你。

words.en: Even really honest people are often made to feel guilty.
words.zh: 即使是真正诚实的人也常常感到内疚。

words.en: The hardened professional smuggler, on the other hand, is never troubled by such feelings, even if he has five hundred gold watches hidden in his suitcase.
words.zh: 而铁石心肠的职业走私犯却从来不会被这种感觉所困扰，即使他的行李箱里藏着五百块金表。

words.en: When I returned from abroad recently, a particularly officious young Customs Officer clearly regarded me as a smuggler.
words.zh: 最近我从国外回来时，一位特别多管闲事的年轻海关官员显然把我视为走私犯。

words.en: 'Have you anything to declare?' he asked, looking me in the eye.
words.zh: “你有什么要申报的吗？”他看着我的眼睛问道。

words.en: 'No,' I answered confidently.
words.zh: “不，”我自信地回答。

words.en: 'Would you mind unlocking this suitcase please? ' 'Not at all,' I answered.
words.zh: “请问您介意打开这个手提箱吗？ ” “一点也不，”我回答道。

words.en: The Officer went through the case with great care.
words.zh: 警官非常仔细地审查了这个案子。

words.en: All the things I had packed so carefully were soon in a dreadful mess.
words.zh: 我精心包装的所有东西很快就变得一团糟。

words.en: I felt sure I would never be able to close the case again.
words.zh: 我确信我再也无法结案了。

words.en: Suddenly, I saw the Officer's face light up.
words.zh: 突然，我看到军官的脸亮了起来。

words.en: He had spotted a tiny bottle at the bottom of my case and he pounced on it with delight.
words.zh: 他在我的箱子底部发现了一个小瓶子，他高兴地扑向它。

words.en: 'Perfume, eh?' he asked sarcastically.
words.zh: “香水，嗯？”他讽刺地问道。

words.en: 'You should have declared that.
words.zh: “你应该这么声明。

words.en: Perfume is not exempt from import duty. ' 'But it isn't perfume, I said.
words.zh: 香水不免征进口税。 ” “但这不是香水，我说。

words.en: 'It's hair gel. ' Then I added with a smile, 'It's a strange mixture I make myself.
words.zh: ‘这是发胶。 ”然后我微笑着补充道，“这是我自己调制的一种奇怪的混合物。

words.en: As I expected, he did not believe me.
words.zh: 正如我所料，他不相信我。

words.en: 'Try it!'
words.zh: “试试吧！”

words.en: I said encouragingly.
words.zh: 我鼓励地说。

words.en: The Officer unscrewed the cap and put the bottle to his nostrils.
words.zh: 警官拧开瓶盖，将瓶子放到鼻孔处。

words.en: He was greeted by an unpleasant smell which convinced him that I was telling the truth.
words.zh: 他闻到一股难闻的气味，这让他相信我说的是实话。

words.en: A few minutes later, I was able to hurry away with precious chalk marks on my baggage.
words.zh: 几分钟后，我就匆匆离开了，行李上还留下了珍贵的粉笔标记。

courses.title: Lesson 12 · Life on a Desert Island

words.en: Most of us have formed an unrealistic picture of life on a desert island.
words.zh: 我们大多数人都对荒岛上的生活形成了不切实际的想象。

words.en: We sometimes imagine a desert island to be a sort of paradise where the sun always shines.
words.zh: 我们有时会把荒岛想象成阳光永远普照的天堂。

words.en: Life there is simple and good.
words.zh: 那里的生活简单而美好。

words.en: Ripe fruit falls from the trees and you never have to work.
words.zh: 成熟的果实从树上掉下来，你永远不需要工作。

words.en: The other side of the picture is quite the opposite.
words.zh: 图片的另一面则恰恰相反。

words.en: Life on a desert island is wretched.
words.zh: 荒岛上的生活是悲惨的。

words.en: You either starve to death or live like Robinson Crusoe, waiting for a boat which never comes.
words.zh: 你要么饿死，要么像鲁滨逊漂流记一样生活，等待一艘永远不会来的船。

words.en: Perhaps there is an element of truth in both these pictures, but few of us have had the opportunity to find out.
words.zh: 也许这两张照片都有一定的真实性，但我们很少有人有机会去发现。

words.en: Two men who recently spent five days on a coral island wished they had stayed there longer.
words.zh: 两名男子最近在珊瑚岛上度过了五天，希望他们能在那里呆更长时间。

words.en: They were taking a badly damaged boat from the Virgin Islands to Miami to have it repaired.
words.zh: 他们正将一艘严重受损的船从维尔京群岛开往迈阿密进行修理。

words.en: During the journey, their boat began to sink.
words.zh: 在旅途中，他们的船开始下沉。

words.en: They quickly loaded a small rubber dinghy with food, matches, and cans of beer and rowed for a few miles across the Caribbean until they arrived at a tiny coral island.
words.zh: 他们很快在一艘小橡皮艇上装满了食物、火柴和啤酒罐，划船横渡加勒比海几英里，最后到达一个小珊瑚岛。

words.en: There were hardly any trees on the island and there was no water, but this did not prove to be a problem.
words.zh: 岛上几乎没有树木，也没有水，但这并没有成为问题。

words.en: The men collected rainwater in the rubber dinghy.
words.zh: 这些人用橡皮艇收集雨水。

words.en: As they had brought a spear gun with them, they had plenty to eat.
words.zh: 因为他们带了矛枪，所以吃的有很多。

words.en: They caught lobster and fish every day, and as one of them put it 'ate like kings'.
words.zh: 他们每天捕捞龙虾和鱼，正如其中一位所说，“吃起来像国王一样”。

words.en: When a passing tanker rescued them five days later, both men were genuinely sorry that they had to leave.
words.zh: 五天后，当一艘路过的油轮救起他们时，两人都对不得不离开感到非常遗憾。

words.en: After her husband had gone to work, Mrs. Richards sent her children to school and went upstairs to her bedroom.
words.zh: 丈夫去上班后，理查兹夫人送孩子们去学校，然后上楼回到自己的卧室。

words.en: She was too excited to do any housework that morning, for in the evening she would be going to a fancy-dress party with her husband.
words.zh: 那天早上她太兴奋了，没有时间做任何家务，因为晚上她要和丈夫一起去参加一个化装舞会。

words.en: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
words.zh: 她本来打算装扮成鬼魂，而服装是前一天晚上做的，所以她迫不及待地想试穿一下。

words.en: Though the costume consisted only of a sheet, it was very effective.
words.zh: 虽然服装只有一张床单，但效果却非常好。

words.en: After putting it on, Mrs. Richards went downstairs.
words.zh: 戴上之后，理查兹夫人下了楼。

words.en: She wanted to find out whether it would be comfortable to wear.
words.zh: 她想看看穿起来是否舒服。

words.en: Just as Mrs. Richards was entering the dining-room, there was a knock on the front door.
words.zh: 正当理查兹夫人走进餐厅时，有人敲前门。

words.en: She knew that it must be the baker.
words.zh: 她知道那一定是面包师。

words.en: She had told him to come straight in if ever she failed to open the door and to leave the bread on the kitchen table.
words.zh: 她告诉他，如果她没开门就直接进来，并将面包留在厨房的桌子上。

words.en: Not wanting to frighten the poor man, Mrs. Richards quickly hid in the small storeroom under the stairs.
words.zh: 理查兹夫人不想吓着这个可怜的人，赶紧躲进了楼梯下的小储藏室里。

words.en: She heard the front door open and heavy footsteps in the hall.
words.zh: 她听到前门打开，大厅里传来沉重的脚步声。

words.en: Suddenly the door of the storeroom was opened and a man entered.
words.zh: 突然，储藏室的门被打开，一个男人走了进来。

words.en: Mrs. Richards realized that it must be the man from the Electricity Board who had come to read the metre.
words.zh: 理查兹夫人意识到一定是电力局的人来抄表的。

words.en: She tried to explain the situation, saying 'It's only me', but it was too late.
words.zh: 她试图解释情况，说“只是我”，但为时已晚。

words.en: The man let out a cry and jumped back several paces.
words.zh: 男子惨叫一声，连连后退数步。

words.en: When Mrs. Richards walked towards him, he fled, slamming the door behind him.
words.zh: 当理查兹夫人朝他走来时，他逃跑了，并关上了身后的门。

words.en: There was a time when the owners of shops and businesses in Chicago had to pay large sums of money to gangsters in return for 'protection'.
words.zh: 曾经有一段时间，芝加哥的商店和企业的老板不得不向歹徒支付大笔金钱以换取“保护”。

words.en: If the money was not paid promptly, the gangsters would quickly put a man out of business by destroying his shop.
words.zh: 如果不及时交钱，歹徒很快就会毁掉一个人的店铺，让他破产。

words.en: Obtaining 'protection money' is not a modern crime.
words.zh: 获取“保护费”并不是现代犯罪。

words.en: As long ago as the fourteenth century, an Englishman, Sir John Hawkwood, made the remarkable discovery that people would rather pay large sums of money than have their life work destroyed by gangsters.
words.zh: 早在十四世纪，英国人约翰·霍克伍德爵士就有了一个非凡的发现：人们宁愿付出大笔金钱，也不愿毕生的心血被歹徒毁掉。

words.en: Six hundred years ago, Sir John Hawkwood arrived in Italy with a band of soldiers and settled near Florence.
words.zh: 六百年前，约翰·霍克伍德爵士率领一队士兵抵达意大利，并在佛罗伦萨附近定居。

words.en: He soon made a name for himself and came to be known to the Italians as Giovanni Acuto.
words.zh: 他很快就出名了，意大利人称他为乔瓦尼·阿库托（Giovanni Acuto）。

words.en: Whenever the Italian city-states were at war with each other, Hawkwood used to hire his soldiers to princes who were willing to pay the high price he demanded.
words.zh: 每当意大利城邦相互交战时，霍克伍德都会向愿意支付他所要求的高价的王子雇佣他的士兵。

words.en: In times of peace, when business was bad, Hawkwood and his men would march into a city-state, and after burning down a few farms, would offer to go away if protection money was paid to them.
words.zh: 在和平时期，生意不好的时候，霍克伍德和他的部下会进军城邦，烧毁一些农场后，如果给他们保护费，他们就会提出离开。

words.en: Hawkwood made large sums of money in this way.
words.zh: 霍克伍德就这样赚了大笔钱。

words.en: In spite of this, the Italians regarded him as a sort of hero.
words.zh: 尽管如此，意大利人仍将他视为英雄。

words.en: When he died at the age of eighty, the Florentines gave him a state funeral and had a picture painted which was dedicated to the memory of 'the most valiant soldier and most notable leader, Signor Giovanni Haukodue'.
words.zh: 当他八十岁时去世时，佛罗伦萨人为他举行了国葬，并为他画了一幅画，以纪念“最英勇的士兵和最著名的领导人乔瓦尼·豪科杜先生”。

courses.title: Lesson 15 · Fifty Pence Worth of Trouble

words.en: Children always appreciate small gifts of money.
words.zh: 孩子们总是喜欢小钱礼物。

words.en: Mum or dad, of course, provides a regular supply of pocket money, but uncles and aunts are always a source of extra income.
words.zh: 当然，妈妈或爸爸会定期提供零用钱，但叔叔阿姨总是额外收入的来源。

words.en: With some children, small sums go a long way.
words.zh: 对于一些孩子来说，少量的钱就可以发挥很大的作用。

words.en: If fifty pence pieces are not exchanged for sweets, they rattle for months inside money boxes.
words.zh: 如果五十便士不能换成糖果，它们就会在钱箱里嘎嘎作响几个月。

words.en: Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a money box.
words.zh: 只有非常节俭的孩子才能装满钱箱。

words.en: For most of them, fifty pence is a small price to pay for a nice big bar of chocolate.
words.zh: 对于他们中的大多数人来说，五十便士对于买一大块美味的巧克力来说只是一个很小的价格。

words.en: My nephew, George, has a money box but it is always empty.
words.zh: 我的侄子乔治有一个钱箱，但它总是空的。

words.en: Very few of the fifty pence pieces and pound coins I have given him have found their way there.
words.zh: 我给他的五十便士和一英镑硬币中很少有找到那里的。

words.en: I gave him fifty pence yesterday and advised him to save it.
words.zh: 昨天我给了他五十便士，并建议他存起来。

words.en: Instead, he bought himself fifty pence worth of trouble.
words.zh: 相反，他给自己带来了价值五十便士的麻烦。

words.en: On his way to the sweet shop, he dropped his fifty pence and it bounced along the pavement and then disappeared down a drain.
words.zh: 在去糖果店的路上，他掉了五十便士，它沿着人行道弹跳起来，然后消失在下水道里。

words.en: George took off his jacket, rolled up his sleeves and pushed his right arm through the drain cover.
words.zh: 乔治脱下夹克，卷起袖子，将右臂伸进排水沟盖。

words.en: He could not find his 50 pence piece anywhere, and what is more, he could not get his arm out.
words.zh: 他到处都找不到他的 50 便士硬币，而且他的手臂也抽不出来。

words.en: A crowd of people gathered round him and a lady rubbed his arm with soap and butter, but George was firmly stuck.
words.zh: 一群人聚集在他周围，一位女士用肥皂和黄油擦拭他的手臂，但乔治被牢牢地卡住了。

words.en: The fire brigade was called and two fire fighters freed George using a special type of grease.
words.zh: 消防队被叫来，两名消防员使用一种特殊类型的油脂救出了乔治。

words.en: George was not too upset by his experience because the lady who owns the sweet shop heard about his troubles and rewarded him with a large box of chocolates.
words.zh: 乔治并没有对他的经历感到太难过，因为糖果店的老板娘听说了他的烦恼，并奖励了他一大盒巧克力。

courses.title: Lesson 16 · Mary Had a Little Lamb

words.en: Mary and her husband Dimitri lived in the tiny village of Perachora in southern Greece.
words.zh: 玛丽和她的丈夫迪米特里住在希腊南部的佩拉乔拉小村庄。

words.en: One of Mary's prize possessions was a little white lamb which her husband had given her.
words.zh: 玛丽最珍贵的财产之一是她丈夫送给她的一只小白羊羔。

words.en: She kept it tied to a tree in a field during the day and went to fetch it every evening.
words.zh: 她白天把它绑在田野里的一棵树上，每天晚上去取它。

words.en: One evening, however the lamb was missing.
words.zh: 然而一天晚上，小羊不见了。

words.en: The rope had been cut, so it was obvious that the lamb had been stolen.
words.zh: 绳子已经断了，很明显羊肉是被偷了。

words.en: When Dimitri came in from the fields, his wife told him what had happened.
words.zh: 当迪米特里从田里回来时，他的妻子告诉他发生了什么事。

words.en: Dimitri at once set out to find the thief.
words.zh: 迪米特里立即出发寻找小偷。

words.en: He knew it would not prove difficult in such a small village.
words.zh: 他知道在这么一个小村庄里这并不困难。

words.en: After telling several of his friends about the theft, Dimitri found out that his neighbour, Aleko, had suddenly acquired a new lamb.
words.zh: 在向几个朋友讲述了这起盗窃事件后，迪米特里发现他的邻居阿列科突然获得了一只新羔羊。

words.en: Dimitri immediately went to Aleko's house and angrily accused him of stealing the lamb.
words.zh: 迪米特里立即前往阿莱科家，愤怒地指责他偷了羔羊。

words.en: He told him he had better return it or he would call the police.
words.zh: 他告诉他最好将其归还，否则他会报警。

words.en: Aleko denied taking it and led Dimitri into his backyard.
words.zh: 阿莱科否认拿走了它，并把迪米特里带进了他的后院。

words.en: It was true that he had just bought a lamb he explained, but his lamb was black.
words.zh: 他解释说，他确实刚买了一只羔羊，但他的羔羊是黑色的。

words.en: Ashamed of having acted so rashly, Dimitri apologized to Aleko for having accused him.
words.zh: 迪米特里为自己如此鲁莽的行为感到羞愧，他向阿莱科道歉，因为他指责了他。

words.en: While they were talking it began to rain and Dimitri stayed in Aleko's house until the rain stopped.
words.zh: 他们说话的时候天开始下雨了，迪米特里留在阿列科的家里直到雨停。

words.en: When he went outside half an hour later, he was astonished to find that the little black lamb was almost white.
words.zh: 半个小时后，当他走到外面时，他惊讶地发现，那只黑色的小羊羔几乎是白色的。

words.en: Its wool, which had been dyed black, had been washed clean by the rain!
words.zh: 原本被染成黑色的羊毛，已经被雨水冲刷干净了！

courses.title: Lesson 17 · The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World
courses.sourceFile: 17－The Longest Suspension Bridge in the World.lrc

words.en: Verrazano, an Italian about whom little is known, sailed into New York Harbour in 1524 and named it Angouleme.
words.zh: 维拉扎诺 (Verrazano) 是一位鲜为人知的意大利人，他于 1524 年驶入纽约港，并将其命名为安古莱姆 (Angouleme)。

words.en: He described it as 'a very agreeable situation located within two small hills in the midst of which flowed a great river.'
words.zh: 他将其描述为“位于两座小山内的一个非常宜人的环境，山间流淌着一条大河。”

words.en: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal, for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
words.zh: 尽管维拉扎诺绝不被认为是一位伟大的探险家，但他的名字可能会永垂不朽，因为 1964 年 11 月 21 日，世界上最长的吊桥以他的名字命名。

words.en: The Verrazano Bridge, which was designed by Othmar Ammann, joins Brooklyn to Staten Island.
words.zh: 维拉扎诺大桥由奥特马尔·阿曼 (Othmar Ammann) 设计，连接布鲁克林和史泰登岛。

words.en: It has a span of 4,260 feet.
words.zh: 它的跨度为 4,260 英尺。

words.en: The bridge is so long that the shape of the earth had to be taken into account by its designer.
words.zh: 这座桥太长了，其设计者必须考虑到地球的形状。

words.en: Two great towers support four huge cables.
words.zh: 两座巨大的塔支撑着四根巨大的电缆。

words.en: The towers are built on immense underwater platforms made of steel and concrete.
words.zh: 这些塔建在由钢铁和混凝土制成的巨大水下平台上。

words.en: The platforms extend to a depth of over 100 feet under the sea.
words.zh: 这些平台延伸至海底100多英尺的深度。

words.en: These alone took sixteen months to build.
words.zh: 仅这些就花了十六个月的时间建造。

words.en: Above the surface of the water, the towers rise to a height of nearly 700 feet.
words.zh: 塔楼露出水面的高度接近 700 英尺。

words.en: They support the cables from which the bridge has been suspended.
words.zh: 它们支撑着悬挂桥梁的缆索。

words.en: Each of the four cables contains 26,108 lengths of wire.
words.zh: 四根电缆中的每根都包含 26,108 根电线。

words.en: It has been estimated that if the bridge were packed with cars, it would still only be carrying a third of its total capacity.
words.zh: 据估计，如果这座桥挤满了汽车，它的承载能力仍然只有其总容量的三分之一。

words.en: However, size and strength are not the only important things about this bridge.
words.zh: 然而，尺寸和强度并不是这座桥唯一重要的因素。

words.en: Despite its immensity, it is both simple and elegant, fulfilling its designer's dream to creat 'an enormous object drawn as faintly as possible'.
words.zh: 尽管它巨大，但它既简单又优雅，实现了设计师的梦想，即创造“一个尽可能淡化的巨大物体”。

courses.title: Lesson 18 · Electric Currents in Modern Art

words.en: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
words.zh: 现代雕塑很少再给我们带来惊喜。

words.en: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
words.zh: 现代艺术只能在博物馆里看到的想法是错误的。

words.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
words.zh: 即使对艺术不感兴趣的人也会注意到公共场所展出的现代雕塑的例子。

words.en: Strange forms stand in gardens, and outside buildings and shops.
words.zh: 花园、建筑物和商店外都有奇怪的形状。

words.en: We have got quite used to them.
words.zh: 我们已经很习惯他们了。

words.en: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
words.zh: 一些所谓的“现代”作品已经展出了近八十年。

words.en: In spite of this, some people — including myself — were surprised by a recent exhibition of modern sculpture.
words.zh: 尽管如此，一些人——包括我自己——对最近举办的现代雕塑展感到惊讶。

words.en: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said: 'Do not touch the exhibits, some of them are dangerous!'
words.zh: 当我进入美术馆时，我首先看到的是一个告示，上面写着：“请勿触摸展品，其中一些展品是危险的！”

words.en: The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture.
words.zh: 展出的物品是移动的雕塑作品。

words.en: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended from the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.
words.zh: 每个人都非常熟悉悬挂在天花板上并随着一阵风而移动的奇怪形状的形式。

words.en: These objects, however, were different.
words.zh: 然而，这些物体是不同的。

words.en: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.
words.zh: 靠墙排列着细长的电线，连接在金属球上。

words.en: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
words.zh: 这些球体一直被磁化并相互吸引或排斥。

words.en: In the centre of the hall, there were a number of tall structures which contained coloured lights.
words.zh: 大厅的中央，矗立着一座座高大的建筑，里面闪烁着彩色的光芒。

words.en: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.
words.zh: 这些灯不停地闪烁，就像发疯的红绿灯一样。

words.en: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
words.zh: 小黑盒子里冒出火花，红灯愤怒地忽明忽暗。

words.en: It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
words.zh: 这有点像史前电子设备的展览。

words.en: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!
words.zh: 这些奇特的造型，似乎不仅是为了给人们带来情感上的震撼，更是为了给人一种电击的感觉！

words.en: Kidnappers are rarely interested in animals, but they recently took considerable interest in Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay's cat.
words.zh: 绑匪很少对动物感兴趣，但他们最近对埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人的猫产生了相当大的兴趣。

words.en: Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay, a very wealthy old lady, has shared a flat with her cat, Rastus, for a great many years.
words.zh: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人是一位非常富有的老太太，多年来她一直与她的猫拉斯特斯合租一套公寓。

words.en: Rastus leads an orderly life.
words.zh: 拉斯特斯过着井然有序的生活。

words.en: He usually takes a short walk in the evenings and is always home by seven o'clock.
words.zh: 他通常在晚上散步一小段路，并且总是在七点钟之前回家。

words.en: One evening, however he failed to arrive.
words.zh: 然而一天晚上，他却没有到达。

words.en: Mrs. Ramsay got very worried.
words.zh: 拉姆齐夫人非常担心。

words.en: She looked everywhere for him but could not find him.
words.zh: 她到处寻找他，却找不到他。

words.en: Three days after Rastus' disappearance, Mrs. Ramsay received an anonymous letter.
words.zh: 拉斯特斯失踪三天后，拉姆齐夫人收到一封匿名信。

words.en: The writer stated that Rastus was in safe hands and would be returned immediately if Mrs. Ramsay paid a ransom of ￡1,000.
words.zh: 作者表示，拉斯特斯目前已安全掌握，如果拉姆齐夫人支付 1,000 英镑的赎金，拉斯特斯将立即归还。

words.en: Mrs. Ramsay was instructed to place the money in a cardboard box and to leave it outside her door.
words.zh: 拉姆齐夫人被指示将钱放入一个纸板箱中，然后将其放在门外。

words.en: At first, she decided to go to the police, but fearing that she would never see Rastus again — the letter had made that quite clear — she changed her mind.
words.zh: 起初，她决定去警察局，但由于担心再也见不到拉斯特斯——信中已经说得很清楚了——她改变了主意。

words.en: She withdrew ￡1000 from her bank and followed the kidnapper's instructions.
words.zh: 她从银行取出了 1000 英镑，并按照绑匪的指示进行了操作。

words.en: The next morning, the box had disappeared but Mrs. Ramsay was sure that the kidnapper would keep his word.
words.zh: 第二天早上，盒子不见了，但拉姆齐夫人确信绑匪会信守诺言。

words.en: Sure enough, Rastus arrived punctually at seven o'clock that evening.
words.zh: 果然，拉斯特斯当天晚上七点准时到达。

words.en: He looked very well, though he was rather thirsty, for he drank half a bottle of milk.
words.zh: 他看上去精神很好，虽然有些口渴，因为他喝了半瓶牛奶。

words.en: The police were astounded when Mrs. Ramsay told them what she had done.
words.zh: 当拉姆齐夫人告诉他们她所做的事情时，警察们感到震惊。

words.en: She explained that Rastus was very dear to her.
words.zh: 她解释说，拉斯塔斯对她来说非常亲爱。

words.en: Considering the amount she paid, he was dear in more ways than one!
words.zh: 考虑到她付出的代价，他在很多方面都是亲爱的！

words.en: In 1908 Lord Northcliffe offered a prize of ￡1,000 to the first man who would fly across the English Channel.
words.zh: 1908 年，诺斯克利夫勋爵向第一个飞越英吉利海峡的人颁发了 1,​​000 英镑的奖金。

words.en: Over a year passed before the first attempt was made.
words.zh: 距离第一次尝试已经过去了一年多。

words.en: On July 19th, 1909, in the early morning, Hubert Latham took off from the French coast in his plane the 'Antoinette IV.'
words.zh: 1909 年 7 月 19 日清晨，休伯特·莱瑟姆乘坐他的飞机“安托瓦内特四世”从法国海岸起飞。

words.en: He had travelled only seven miles across the Channel when his engine failed and he was forced to land on the sea.
words.zh: 他只跨过英吉利海峡七英里，引擎就发生故障，被迫在海上降落。

words.en: The 'Antoinette' floated on the water until Latham was picked up by a ship.
words.zh: “安托瓦内特”号漂浮在水面上，直到莱瑟姆被一艘船接走。

words.en: Two days later, Louis Bleriot arrived near Calais with a plane called 'No.XI'.
words.zh: 两天后，路易斯·布莱里奥乘坐一架名为“No.XI”的飞机抵达加来附近。

words.en: Bleriot had been making planes since 1905 and this was his latest model.
words.zh: Bleriot 自 1905 年起就开始制造飞机，这是他的最新型号。

words.en: A week before, he had completed a successful overland flight during which he covered twenty-six miles.
words.zh: 一周前，他成功完成了一次陆上飞行，飞行了二十六英里。

words.en: Latham, however, did not give up easily.
words.zh: 然而，莱瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。

words.en: He, too, arrived near Calais on the same day with a new 'Antoinette'.
words.zh: 同一天，他也带着一辆新的“安托瓦内特”抵达加来附近。

words.en: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.
words.zh: 看起来好像将会有一场激动人心的横渡英吉利海峡比赛。

words.en: Both planes were going to take off on July 25th, but Latham failed to get up early enough.
words.zh: 两架飞机原定于 7 月 25 日起飞，但莱瑟姆起得不够早。

words.en: After making a short test flight at 4.15 a.m., Bleriot set off half an hour later.
words.zh: 凌晨4点15分进行了短暂的试飞后，布莱里奥于半小时后出发。

words.en: His great flight lasted thirty-seven minutes.
words.zh: 他的伟大飞行持续了三十七分钟。

words.en: When he landed near Dover, the first person to greet him was a local policeman.
words.zh: 当他降落在多佛附近时，第一个迎接他的人是当地的警察。

words.en: Latham made another attempt a week later and got within half a mile of Dover, but he was unlucky again.
words.zh: 一周后，莱瑟姆再次尝试，距离多佛不到半英里，但他再次不走运。

words.en: His engine failed and he landed on the sea for the second time.
words.zh: 他的发动机发生故障，他第二次降落在海上。

words.en: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.
words.zh: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英国非常流行。

words.en: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
words.zh: 那时候，拳击手们赤手空拳争夺奖金。

words.en: Because of this, they were known as 'prizefighters'.
words.zh: 因此，他们被称为“职业拳击手”。

words.en: However, boxing was very crude, for there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
words.zh: 然而，拳击运动非常原始，因为没有规则，职业拳击手可能在比赛中受重伤甚至死亡。

words.en: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.
words.zh: 丹尼尔·门多萨 (Daniel Mendoza) 出生于 1764 年，是拳击史上最丰富多彩的人物之一。

words.en: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
words.zh: 直到 1860 年，昆斯伯里侯爵制定了第一套规则，手套的使用才被引入。

words.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
words.zh: 尽管从技术上讲，门多萨是一名职业拳击手，但他为将粗俗的职业拳击变成一项运动做了很多工作，因为他将科学带入了这项运动中。

words.en: In his day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.
words.zh: 在他那个时代，门多萨享有极高的人气。

words.en: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
words.zh: 他受到富人和穷人的崇拜。

words.en: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
words.zh: 门多萨在一场拳击比赛后迅速成名，当时他只有十四岁。

words.en: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.
words.zh: 这引起了当时英格兰最杰出的拳击手理查德·汉弗莱斯的注意。

words.en: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.
words.zh: 他主动提出训练门多萨，他的小学生学得很快。

words.en: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
words.zh: 事实上，门多萨很快就变得如此成功，以至于汉弗里斯转而反对他。

words.en: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.
words.zh: 两人争吵得很厉害，显然只能通过打斗来解决。

words.en: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.
words.zh: 在斯蒂尔顿举行了一场比赛，两人打了一个小时。

words.en: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.
words.zh: 公众在门多萨身上下了重注，但他被击败了。

words.en: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.
words.zh: 门多萨后来在拳击场上遇到了汉弗莱斯，他第二次输掉了比赛。

words.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
words.zh: 直到1790年他的第三场比赛才最终击败汉弗莱斯，成为英格兰冠军。

words.en: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.
words.zh: 与此同时，他创办了一所非常成功的学院，甚至拜伦勋爵也成为他的学生之一。

words.en: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as ￡100 for a single appearance.
words.zh: 他赚了很多钱，一次出场的片酬就高达100英镑。

words.en: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
words.zh: 尽管如此，他却因为挥霍无度，总是负债累累。

words.en: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.
words.zh: 在他被一位名叫绅士杰克逊的拳击手击败后，他很快就被遗忘了。

words.en: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
words.zh: 1836年，他因未能偿还债务而入狱，并在贫困中去世。

words.en: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
words.zh: 有些戏剧非常成功，可以连续上演多年。

words.en: In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
words.zh: 从很多方面来说，这对于那些需要夜复一夜重复相同台词的可怜演员来说是不幸的。

words.en: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
words.zh: 人们会期望他们能够熟记自己的部分，并且永远不会动摇。

words.en: Yet this is not always the case.
words.zh: 但情况并非总是如此。

words.en: A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for twenty years.
words.zh: 一位著名演员曾在一部非常成功的戏剧中扮演一位在巴士底狱被囚禁了二十年的贵族。

words.en: In the last act, a gaoler would always come on to the stage with a letter which he would hand to the prisoner.
words.zh: 在最后一幕中，狱卒总是会带着一封信走上舞台，交给囚犯。

words.en: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
words.zh: 尽管贵族在每次演出时都会宣读这封信，但他始终坚持将其全文写下来。

words.en: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if, after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
words.zh: 一天晚上，狱卒决定跟他的同事开个玩笑，看他经过这么多次的表演，是否能把信中的内容背下来。

words.en: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
words.zh: 戏剧的最后一幕拉开了帷幕，贵族独自坐在黑暗牢房的铁栅后面。

words.en: Just then, the gaoler appeared with the precious letter in his hands.
words.zh: 就在这时，狱卒出现了，手里拿着那封珍贵的信。

words.en: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.
words.zh: 他走进牢房，将信交给贵族。

words.en: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.
words.zh: 但他给他的副本并没有像往常一样写完整。

words.en: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
words.zh: 那只是一张白纸。

words.en: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
words.zh: 看守热切地看着，急切地想看看他的同伴是否终于学会了台词。

words.en: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.
words.zh: 贵族盯着那张白纸看了几秒。

words.en: Then, squinting his eyes, he said: 'The light is dim.
words.zh: 然后，他眯着眼睛说道：“光线昏暗。”

words.en: Read the letter to me.'
words.zh: 把这封信读给我听。

words.en: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the gaoler.
words.zh: 他立即将那张纸递给了狱卒。

words.en: Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either, the gaoler replied: 'The light is indeed dim, sire.
words.zh: 狱卒发现自己也记不住信中的一个字，就回答说：“陛下，光线确实昏暗。”

words.en: I must get my glasses. ' With this, he hurried off the stage.
words.zh: 我必须去拿眼镜。 ”说完，他就匆匆走下了讲台。

words.en: Much to the aristocrat's amusement, the gaoler returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.
words.zh: 让贵族感到很有趣的是，几分钟后，看守带着一副眼镜和通常的那封信回来了，他开始向囚犯宣读这封信。

courses.title: Lesson 23 · One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison
courses.sourceFile: 23－One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison.lrc

words.en: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten.
words.zh: 当人们试图决定什么可以吃、什么不能吃时，他们会变得非常不合逻辑。

words.en: If you lived in the Mediterranean, for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy.
words.zh: 例如，如果你住在地中海，你会认为章鱼是一种美味佳肴。

words.en: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive.
words.zh: 你无法理解为什么有些人会觉得它令人厌恶。

words.en: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat-the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
words.zh: 另一方面，一想到用动物脂肪煎土豆，你的胃就会反胃——这是许多北方国家普遍接受的做法。

words.en: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
words.zh: 可悲的事实是，我们大多数人都是吃某些食物长大的，而且我们一生都坚持吃它们。

words.en: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
words.zh: 没有什么生物比普通的花园蜗牛受到更多的赞扬和虐待。

words.en: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.
words.zh: 用酒烹制的蜗牛在世界各地都是一种奢侈的享受。

words.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
words.zh: 无数人从小就学会将蜗牛与食物联系起来。

words.en: My friend, Robert, lives in a country where snails are despised.
words.zh: 我的朋友罗伯特生活在一个鄙视蜗牛的国家。

words.en: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.
words.zh: 由于他的公寓位于一个大城市，因此他没有自己的花园。

words.en: For years he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
words.zh: 多年来，他一直要求我从我的花园里收集蜗牛并把它们带给他。

words.en: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after a heavy shower, I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
words.zh: 这个想法从来没有对我很有吸引力，但有一天，一场大雨过后，我碰巧在花园里散步，发现大量的蜗牛在我的一些珍贵植物上漫步。

words.en: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
words.zh: 我一时冲动，收集了几十个，装进纸袋，交给罗伯特。

words.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
words.zh: 罗伯特很高兴见到我，也对我的小礼物感到同样满意。

words.en: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
words.zh: 我把包留在大厅里，罗伯特和我走进客厅，我们聊了几个小时。

words.en: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
words.zh: 当罗伯特突然说我必须留下来吃晚饭时，我已经忘记了蜗牛的事。

words.en: Snails would, of course, be the main dish.
words.zh: 蜗牛当然是主菜。

words.en: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.
words.zh: 我不喜欢这个主意，不情愿地跟着罗伯特走出了房间。

words.en: To our dismay, we saw that there were snails everywhere: they had escaped from the paper bag and had taken complete possession of the hall!
words.zh: 令我们沮丧的是，我们看到到处都是蜗牛：它们从纸袋里逃了出来，完全占领了大厅！

words.en: I have never be able to look at a snail since then.
words.zh: 从那以后我再也不敢看蜗牛了。

courses.title: Lesson 24 · A Skeleton in the Cupboard

words.en: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
words.zh: 我们经常在小说中读到，一个看似受人尊敬的人或家庭有一些可怕的秘密，多年来一直对陌生人隐瞒。

words.en: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.
words.zh: 英语中有一个生动的说法来描述这种情况。

words.en: The terrible secret is called 'a skeleton in the cupboard'.
words.zh: 这个可怕的秘密被称为“柜子里的骷髅”。

words.en: At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
words.zh: 在故事中的某个戏剧性时刻，可怕的秘密被人所知，声誉也被毁了。

words.en: The reader's hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine, a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
words.zh: 当读者在小说的最后几页读到女主人公，一位对每个人都那么友善的亲爱的老太太，在年轻时毒死了她的五个丈夫中的每一个时，他的头发都竖起来了。

words.en: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
words.zh: 这样的事情出现在小说中是很好的。

words.en: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn, but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
words.zh: 在不同程度上，我们都有一些秘密，即使我们最亲密的朋友也不想知道这些秘密，但我们中很少有人有秘密。

words.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
words.zh: 我认识的唯一一个在柜子里藏着骷髅的人是乔治·卡尔顿，他对此感到非常自豪。

words.en: George studied medicine in his youth.
words.zh: 乔治年轻时学习医学。

words.en: Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
words.zh: 然而，他并没有成为一名医生，而是成为了一名成功的侦探小说作家。

words.en: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
words.zh: 我曾经在他家度过了一个我永远不会忘记的不舒服的周末。

words.en: George showed me to the guestroom which, he said, was rarely used.
words.zh: 乔治带我参观了客房，他说那里很少有人使用。

words.en: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
words.zh: 他让我把行李打开，然后下来吃晚饭。

words.en: After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang one of the two suits I had brought with me in the cupboard.
words.zh: 当我把衬衫和内衣堆放在两个空抽屉里后，我决定把带来的两套西装中的一套挂在橱柜里。

words.en: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
words.zh: 我打开柜门，站在门前，惊呆了。

words.en: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
words.zh: 一具骷髅在我眼前晃来晃去。

words.en: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
words.zh: 门突然一动，让它轻轻摇晃起来，给我的感觉是它要向我扑来。

words.en: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
words.zh: 我扔下西装，冲下楼去告诉乔治。

words.en: This was worse than 'a terrible secret'; this was a real skeleton!
words.zh: 这比“一个可怕的秘密”还要糟糕。这是一具真正的骷髅！

words.en: But George was unsympathetic.
words.zh: 但乔治却毫无同情心。

words.en: 'Oh, that,' he said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
words.zh: “哦，那个，”他微笑着说，好像在谈论一位老朋友。

words.en: 'That's Sebastian.
words.zh: “那是塞巴斯蒂安。

words.en: You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.'
words.zh: 你忘了我曾经是一名医科学生。

words.en: One of the most famous sailing ships of the nineteenth century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greenwich.
words.zh: 十九世纪最著名的帆船之一卡蒂萨克号仍然可以在格林威治看到。

words.en: She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.
words.zh: 她矗立在干燥的土地上，每年都有成千上万的人来参观。

words.en: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
words.zh: 她令人印象深刻地提醒人们过去的伟大船只。

words.en: Before they were replaced by steamships, sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
words.zh: 在被轮船取代之前，像卡蒂萨克号这样的帆船被用来从中国运输茶叶和从澳大利亚运输羊毛。

words.en: The Cutty Sark was one of the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.
words.zh: 卡蒂萨克号是有史以来建造的速度最快的帆船之一。

words.en: The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
words.zh: 唯一与她相匹配的另一艘船是温泉关号。

words.en: Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872 on an exciting race to England.
words.zh: 1872 年 6 月 18 日，这两艘船从上海出发，开始了前往英国的激动人心的航行。

words.en: This race, which went on for exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
words.zh: 这场比赛持续了整整四个月，是同类比赛中的最后一场。

words.en: It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
words.zh: 它标志着有帆船舶这一伟大传统的结束和新时代的开始。

words.en: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae, but on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.
words.zh: 比赛开始后，两艘船中第一艘抵达爪哇的是温泉关号，但在印度洋，卡蒂萨克号领先。

words.en: It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home, but during the race she had a lot of bad luck.
words.zh: 看起来她肯定会成为第一艘回家的船，但在比赛期间她却运气不佳。

words.en: In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm during which her rudder was torn away.
words.zh: 八月，她遭遇了一场非常猛烈的风暴，船舵被撕裂。

words.en: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
words.zh: 卡蒂萨克号左右摇晃，无法操纵她的方向。

words.en: A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks and it was fitted with great difficulty.
words.zh: 船上用备用木板做了一个临时舵，安装起来非常困难。

words.en: This greatly reduced the speed of the ship, for there was a danger that if she travelled too quickly, this rudder would be torn away as well.
words.zh: 这大大降低了船的速度，因为如果行驶得太快，船舵就有被撕裂的危险。

words.en: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
words.zh: 因此，卡蒂萨克号失去了领先优势。

words.en: After crossing the Equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted, but by now the Thermopylae was over five hundred miles ahead.
words.zh: 穿越赤道后，船长在港口打电话安装新舵，但此时温泉关已经领先五百多英里。

words.en: Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
words.zh: 尽管新舵以极快的速度安装完毕，但卡蒂萨克号仍不可能获胜。

words.en: She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
words.zh: 她在温泉关后一周抵达英国。

words.en: Even this was remarkable, considering that she had had so many delays.
words.zh: 考虑到她已经耽搁了这么多次，即使这样也很了不起。

words.en: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
words.zh: 毫无疑问，如果她没有失去舵，她会轻松赢得比赛。

courses.title: Lesson 26 · Wanted: a Large Biscuit Tin

words.en: No one can avoid being influenced by advertisements.
words.zh: 没有人能够避免受到广告的影响。

words.en: Much as we may pride ourselves on our good taste, we are no longer free to choose the things we want, for advertising exerts a subtle influence on us.
words.zh: 尽管我们可能为自己的良好品味感到自豪，但我们不再可以自由选择我们想要的东西，因为广告对我们产生了微妙的影响。

words.en: In their efforts to persuade us to buy this or that product, advertisers have made a close study of human nature and have classified all our little weaknesses.
words.zh: 广告商在努力说服我们购买这个或那个产品时，对人性进行了仔细研究，并对我们所有的小弱点进行了分类。

words.en: Advertisers discovered years ago that all of us love to get something for nothing.
words.zh: 广告商多年前就发现我们所有人都喜欢不劳而获。

words.en: An advertisement which begins with the magic word FREE can rarely go wrong.
words.zh: 以“免费”这个神奇词开头的广告很少会出错。

words.en: These days, advertisers not only offer free samples, but free cars, free houses, and free trips round the world as well.
words.zh: 如今，广告商不仅提供免费样品，还提供免费汽车、免费房屋和免费环游世界。

words.en: They devise hundreds of competitions which will enable us to win huge sums of money.
words.zh: 他们设计了数百场比赛，这将使我们能够赢得巨额奖金。

words.en: Radio and television have made it possible for advertisers to capture the attention of millions of people in this way.
words.zh: 广播和电视使广告商能够通过这种方式吸引数百万人的注意力。

words.en: During a radio programme, a company of biscuit manufacturers once asked listeners to bake biscuits and send them to their factory.
words.zh: 在一个广播节目中，一家饼干制造商公司曾经要求听众烘烤饼干并将其送到他们的工厂。

words.en: They offered to pay $10 a pound for the biggest biscuit baked by a listener.
words.zh: 他们愿意支付每磅 10 美元购买听众烤制的最大的饼干。

words.en: The response to this competition was tremendous.
words.zh: 此次比赛反响热烈。

words.en: Before long, biscuits of all shapes and sizes began arriving at the factory.
words.zh: 不久之后，各种形状和大小的饼干开始抵达工厂。

words.en: One lady brought biscuit on a wheelbarrow.
words.zh: 一位女士用独轮车带来了饼干。

words.en: It weighed nearly 500 pounds.
words.zh: 它重近500磅。

words.en: A little later, a man came along with a biscuit which occupied the whole boot of his car.
words.zh: 过了一会儿，一个男人带着一块饼干走了过来，饼干占据了他整个车的后备箱。

words.en: All the biscuits that were sent were carefully weighed.
words.zh: 所有送来的饼干都经过仔细称重。

words.en: The largest was 713 pounds.
words.zh: 最大的重达713磅。

words.en: It seemed certain that this would win the prize.
words.zh: 看来这次获奖是肯定的。

words.en: But just before the competition closed, a lorry arrived at the factory with a truly colossal biscuit which weighed 2,400 pounds.
words.zh: 但就在比赛结束前，一辆卡车载着一块重达 2,400 磅的巨型饼干抵达工厂。

words.en: It had been baked by a college student who had used over 1,000 pounds of flour, 800 pounds of sugar, 200 pounds of fat, and 400 pounds of various other ingredients.
words.zh: 它是由一名大学生烘焙的，他使用了 1000 磅面粉、800 磅糖、200 磅脂肪和 400 磅各种其他成分。

words.en: It was so heavy that a crane had to be used to remove it from the lorry.
words.zh: 它太重了，必须使用起重机才能将其从卡车上卸下。

words.en: The manufacturers had to pay more money than they had anticipated, for they bought the biscuit from the student for $24,000.
words.zh: 制造商不得不支付比他们预期更多的钱，因为他们以 24,000 美元从学生那里购买了饼干。

courses.title: Lesson 27 · Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy
courses.sourceFile: 27－Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy.lrc

words.en: It has been said that everyone lives by selling something.
words.zh: 有人说，每个人都靠卖东西生活。

words.en: In the light of this statement, teachers live by selling knowledge, philosophers by selling wisdom and priests by selling spiritual comfort.
words.zh: 由此看来，教师靠出卖知识而生存，哲学家靠出卖智慧而生存，牧师靠出卖精神安慰而生存。

words.en: Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money, it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
words.zh: 尽管可以用金钱来衡量物质商品的价值，但要估计人们为我们提供的服务的真实价值却极其困难。

words.en: There are times when we would willingly give everything we possess to save our lives, yet we might grudge paying a surgeon a high fee for offering us precisely this service.
words.zh: 有时，我们愿意付出我们所拥有的一切来挽救我们的生命，但我们可能不愿意向外科医生支付高额费用，因为他们为我们提供了这种服务。

words.en: The conditions of society are such that skills have to be paid for in the same way that goods are paid for at a shop.
words.zh: 社会条件是技能必须像在商店支付商品一样支付费用。

words.en: Everyone has something to sell.
words.zh: 每个人都有东西要卖。

words.en: Tramps seem to be the only exception to this general rule.
words.zh: 流浪汉似乎是这条一般规则的唯一例外。

words.en: Beggars almost sell themselves as human beings to arouse the pity of passers-by.
words.zh: 乞丐几乎出卖自己为人，以引起路人的怜悯。

words.en: But real tramps are not beggars.
words.zh: 但真正的流浪汉并不是乞丐。

words.en: They have nothing to sell and require nothing from others.
words.zh: 他们没有什么可卖的，也不需要别人提供任何东西。

words.en: In seeking independence, they do not sacrifice their human dignity.
words.zh: 在寻求独立的过程中，他们不会牺牲自己的人格尊严。

words.en: A tramp may ask you for money, but he will never ask you to feel sorry for him.
words.zh: 流浪汉可能会向你要钱，但他绝不会要求你为他感到难过。

words.en: He has deliberately chosen to lead the life he leads and is fully aware of the consequences.
words.zh: 他有意选择过自己现在的生活，并且完全清楚其后果。

words.en: He may never be sure where the next meal is coming from, but he is free from the thousands of anxieties which afflict other people.
words.zh: 他可能永远不确定下一顿饭从哪里来，但他摆脱了困扰其他人的数千种焦虑。

words.en: His few material possessions make it possible for him to move from place to place with ease.
words.zh: 他的物质财富不多，这使他能够轻松地从一个地方搬到另一个地方。

words.en: By having to sleep in the open, he gets far closer to the world of nature than most of us ever do.
words.zh: 由于必须在露天睡觉，他比我们大多数人都更接近自然世界。

words.en: He may hunt, beg, or steal occasionally to keep himself alive; he may even, in times of real need, do a little work; but he will never sacrifice his freedom.
words.zh: 他偶尔会打猎、乞讨或偷窃来维持自己的生命。在真正需要的时候，他甚至可以做一点工作；但他永远不会牺牲他的自由。

words.en: We often speak of tramps with contempt and put them in the same class as beggars, but how many of us can honestly say that we have not felt a little envious of their simple way of life and their freedom from care?
words.zh: 我们常常轻蔑地谈论流浪汉，将他们与乞丐归为同一类，但我们当中有多少人能诚实地说，我们没有对他们简单的生活方式和无忧无虑的生活感到羡慕呢？

words.en: Small boats loaded with wares sped to the great liner as she was entering the harbour.
words.zh: 当这艘大客轮驶入港口时，满载货物的小船快速驶向她。

words.en: Before she had anchored, the men from the boats had climbed on board and the decks were soon covered with colourful rugs from Persia, silks from India, copper coffee pots, and beautiful handmade silverware.
words.zh: 在她抛锚之前，船上的人就已经爬上船了，甲板上很快就铺满了来自波斯的彩色地毯、来自印度的丝绸、铜咖啡壶和漂亮的手工银器。

words.en: It was difficult not to be tempted.
words.zh: 很难不被诱惑。

words.en: Many of the tourists on board had begun bargaining with the tradesmen, but I decided not to buy anything until I had disembarked.
words.zh: 船上的许多游客已经开始与商人讨价还价，但我决定在下船之前不买任何东西。

words.en: I had no sooner got off the ship than I was assailed by a man who wanted to sell me a diamond ring.
words.zh: 我刚下船，就被一个想卖给我钻戒的人袭击了。

words.en: I had no intention of buying one, but I could not conceal the fact that I was impressed by the size of the diamonds.
words.zh: 我无意购买一颗，但我无法掩饰钻石的大小给我留下了深刻的印象。

words.en: Some of them were as big as marbles.
words.zh: 其中一些像弹珠一样大。

words.en: The man went to great lengths to prove that the diamonds were real.
words.zh: 该男子竭尽全力证明这些钻石是真的。

words.en: As we were walking past a shop, he held a diamond firmly against the window and made a deep impression in the glass.
words.zh: 当我们路过一家商店时，他将一颗钻石紧紧地靠在窗户上，在玻璃上留下了深刻的印象。

words.en: It took me over half an hour to get rid of him.
words.zh: 我花了半个多小时才摆脱他。

words.en: The next man to approach me was selling expensive pens and watches.
words.zh: 下一个接近我的人正在销售昂贵的钢笔和手表。

words.en: I examined one of the pens closely.
words.zh: 我仔细检查了其中一支笔。

words.en: It certainly looked genuine.
words.zh: 它看起来确实是真的。

words.en: At the base of the gold cap, the words 'made in the U.S.A.' had been neatly inscribed.
words.zh: 金盖底部刻有“Made in U.S.A.”字样被工整地铭刻着。

words.en: The man said that the pen was worth ￡50, but as a special favour, he would let me have it for ￡30.
words.zh: 那人说这支笔值50英镑，但作为特殊恩惠，他愿意以30英镑的价格给我。

words.en: I shook my head and held up five fingers indicating that I was willing to pay ￡5.
words.zh: 我摇摇头，举起五个手指表示我愿意付5英镑。

words.en: Gesticulating wildly, the man acted as if he found my offer outrageous, but he eventually reduced the price to 10 pounds.
words.zh: 那人疯狂地比划着，好像他觉得我的报价太离谱了，但他最终还是把价格降到了 10 英镑。

words.en: Shrugging my shoulders I began to walk away when, a moment later, he ran after me and thrust the pen into my hands.
words.zh: 我耸耸肩开始走开，过了一会儿，他追上我，把笔塞到我手里。

words.en: Though he kept throwing up his arms in despair, he readily accepted the ￡5 I gave him.
words.zh: 尽管他不断地绝望地举起双臂，但他还是欣然接受了我给他的5英镑。

words.en: I felt especially pleased with my wonderful bargain — until I got back to the ship.
words.zh: 我对这次划算的交易感到特别满意——直到我回到船上。

words.en: No matter how hard I tried, it was impossible to fill this beautiful pen with ink and to this day it has never written a single word!
words.zh: 无论我如何努力，这支漂亮的钢笔都无法沾满墨水，至今也没有写出一个字！

words.en: Whether we find a joke funny or not largely depends on where we have been brought up.
words.zh: 我们是否觉得一个笑话好笑很大程度上取决于我们在哪里长大。

words.en: The sense of humour is mysteriously bound up with national characteristics.
words.zh: 幽默感与民族特色有着神秘的联系。

words.en: A Frenchman, for instance, might find it hard to laugh at a Russian joke.
words.zh: 例如，一个法国人可能会发现很难因为俄罗斯的笑话而发笑。

words.en: In the same way, a Russian might fail to see anything amusing in a joke which would make an Englishman laugh to tears.
words.zh: 同样，俄罗斯人可能看不出一个能让英国人笑得流泪的笑话有什么好笑的地方。

words.en: Most funny stories are based on comic situations.
words.zh: 大多数有趣的故事都是基于喜剧场景。

words.en: In spite of national differences, certain funny situations have a universal appeal.
words.zh: 尽管存在国家差异，但某些有趣的情况具有普遍吸引力。

words.en: No matter where you live, you would find it difficult not to laugh at, say, Charlie Chaplin's early films.
words.zh: 无论你住在哪里，你都会发现很难不嘲笑查理·卓别林的早期电影。

words.en: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from U.S., has recently come into fashion.
words.zh: 然而，一种主要源自美国的新型幽默最近开始流行。

words.en: It is called 'sick humour'.
words.zh: 这被称为“病态幽默”。

words.en: Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.
words.zh: 喜剧演员的笑话以暴力死亡或严重事故等悲惨情况为基础。

words.en: Many people find this sort of joke distasteful.
words.zh: 很多人都觉得这种笑话令人反感。

words.en: The following example of 'sick humour' will enable you to judge for yourself.
words.zh: 以下“病态幽默”的例子将使您能够自行判断。

words.en: A man who had broken his right leg was taken to hospital a few weeks before Christmas.
words.zh: 圣诞节前几周，一名右腿骨折的男子被送往医院。

words.en: From the moment he arrived there, he kept on pestering his doctor to tell him when he would be able to go home.
words.zh: 从到达那里的那一刻起，他就一直缠着医生告诉他什么时候可以回家。

words.en: He dreaded having to spend Christmas in hospital.
words.zh: 他害怕必须在医院度过圣诞节。

words.en: Though the doctor did his best, the patient's recovery was slow.
words.zh: 尽管医生尽了最大努力，病人的康复还是很缓慢。

words.en: On Christmas day, the man still had his right leg in plaster.
words.zh: 圣诞节那天，这名男子的右腿仍然打着石膏。

words.en: He spent a miserable day in bed thinking of all the fun he was missing.
words.zh: 他在床上度过了痛苦的一天，想着他错过的所有乐趣。

words.en: The following day, however, the doctor consoled him by telling him that his chances of being able to leave hospital in time for New Year celebrations were good.
words.zh: 然而第二天，医生安慰他，告诉他，他能够及时出院庆祝新年的机会很大。

words.en: The man took heart and sure enough, on New Year's Eve he was able to hobble along to a party.
words.zh: 男人精神一振，果然除夕夜他能一瘸一拐地去参加一个聚会。

words.en: To compensate for his unpleasant experiences in hospital, the man drank a little more than was good for him.
words.zh: 为了弥补在医院的不愉快经历，该男子喝得比对他有益的多了一点。

words.en: In the process, he enjoyed himself thoroughly and kept telling everybody how much he hated hospitals.
words.zh: 在这个过程中，他玩得很开心，并不停地告诉大家他有多么讨厌医院。

words.en: He was still mumbling something about hospitals at the end of the party when he slipped on a piece of ice and broke his left leg.
words.zh: 聚会结束时，他还在嘀咕一些关于医院的事情，突然在一块冰上滑倒，摔断了左腿。

courses.title: Lesson 30 · The Death of a Ghost

words.en: For years, villagers believed that Endley farm was haunted.
words.zh: 多年来，村民们一直认为恩德利农场闹鬼。

words.en: The farm was owned by two brothers, Joe and Bob Cox.
words.zh: 该农场由乔·考克斯和鲍勃·考克斯两兄弟所有。

words.en: They employed a few farmhands, but no one was willing to work there long.
words.zh: 他们雇用了一些农场工人，但没有人愿意在那里工作很长时间。

words.en: Every time a worker gave up his job, he told the same story.
words.zh: 每当有工人放弃工作时，他都会讲述同样的故事。

words.en: Farm labourers said that they always woke up to find that work had been done overnight.
words.zh: 农场工人说，他们总是一觉醒来，发现工作已经在一夜之间完成了。

words.en: Hay had been cut and cowsheds had been cleaned.
words.zh: 干草已经割完，牛棚也已经打扫干净。

words.en: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.
words.zh: 一名彻夜未眠的农场工人声称看到一个人影在月光下割玉米。

words.en: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.
words.zh: 随着时间的推移，考克斯兄弟雇佣了一个尽职尽责的幽灵来为他们完成大部分工作，这已成为一个公认的事实。

words.en: No one suspected that there might be someone else on the farm who had never been seen.
words.zh: 没有人怀疑农场里可能还有其他从未见过的人。

words.en: This was indeed the case.
words.zh: 事实确实如此。

words.en: A short time ago, villagers were astonished to learn that the ghost of Endley had died.
words.zh: 不久前，村民们惊讶地发现恩德利的鬼魂已经死了。

words.en: Everyone went to the funeral, for the 'ghost' was none other than Eric Cox, a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
words.zh: 每个人都参加了葬礼，因为“鬼魂”不是别人，正是埃里克·考克斯，他的三弟，本应年轻时就去世了。

words.en: After the funeral, Joe and Bob revealed a secret which they had kept for over fifty years.
words.zh: 葬礼结束后，乔和鲍勃透露了他们保守了五十多年的秘密。

words.en: Eric had been the eldest son of the family, very much older than his two brothers.
words.zh: 埃里克是家里的长子，比他的两个兄弟年长很多。

words.en: He had been obliged to join the army during the Second World War.
words.zh: 第二次世界大战期间，他被迫参军。

words.en: As he hated army life, he decided to desert his regiment.
words.zh: 由于他讨厌军队生活，他决定开小差。

words.en: When he learnt that he would be sent abroad, he returned to the farm and his father hid him until the end of the war.
words.zh: 当他得知自己将被送往国外时，他回到了农场，父亲把他藏起来，直到战争结束。

words.en: Fearing the authorities, Eric remained in hiding after the war as well.
words.zh: 由于害怕当局，埃里克在战后也一直躲藏起来。

words.en: His father told everybody that Eric had been killed in action.
words.zh: 他的父亲告诉所有人埃里克在战斗中阵亡。

words.en: The only other people who knew the secret were Joe and Bob.
words.zh: 唯一知道这个秘密的人是乔和鲍勃。

words.en: They did not even tell their wives.
words.zh: 他们甚至没有告诉他们的妻子。

words.en: When their father died they thought it their duty to keep Eric in hiding.
words.zh: 当他们的父亲去世后，他们认为有责任让埃里克躲起来。

words.en: All these years, Eric had lived as a recluse.
words.zh: 这些年来，埃里克一直过着隐居的生活。

words.en: He used to sleep during the day and work at night, quite unaware of the fact that he had become the ghost of Endley.
words.zh: 他白天睡觉，晚上工作，完全没有意识到自己已经成为恩德利的鬼魂。

words.en: When he died, however, his brothers found it impossible to keep the secret any longer.
words.zh: 然而，当他去世后，他的兄弟们发现不可能再保守这个秘密了。

words.en: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
words.zh: 真正的怪人从来不会故意去引起别人的注意。

words.en: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
words.zh: 他们无视社会习俗，却没有意识到自己正在做任何非凡的事情。

words.en: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
words.zh: 这总是为他们赢得他人的爱和尊重，因为他们为平淡的日常生活增添了色彩。

words.en: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
words.zh: 在理查德·科尔森去世之前，他一直是我们镇上最著名的人物之一。

words.en: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman, but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
words.zh: 他是一位精明而富有的商人，但镇上的大多数人对他生活的这一面却几乎一无所知。

words.en: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
words.zh: 我们大家都知道他叫迪基，早在他去世之前，他的古怪就已经成为传奇。

words.en: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
words.zh: 迪基非常不喜欢势利小人。

words.en: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
words.zh: 尽管他拥有一辆大汽车，但他很少使用它，总是喜欢步行。

words.en: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
words.zh: 即使下大雨，他也不肯带伞。

words.en: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
words.zh: 有一天，他淋了一场特别大的雨，走进了一家昂贵的商店。

words.en: He wanted to buy a ￡300 watch for his wife, but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
words.zh: 他想给妻子买一块300英镑的手表，但他的身体脏兮兮的，以至于助理拒绝为他服务。

words.en: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
words.zh: 迪基一言不发地离开了商店，拎着一个大布袋回来了。

words.en: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
words.zh: 由于它太重了，他把它扔在柜台上。

words.en: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
words.zh: 助理让他离开，但迪基没有理他，并要求见经理。

words.en: Recognizing who the customer was, the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
words.zh: 经理认出顾客是谁后，非常抱歉，并严厉斥责了助理。

words.en: When Dickie was given the watch, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
words.zh: 当迪基收到手表时，他把布袋递给了助理。

words.en: It contained ￡300 in pennies.
words.zh: 里面有 300 英镑的便士。

words.en: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left — 30,000 pennies in all!
words.zh: 他坚持要助理在走之前数一下钱——一共三万便士！

words.en: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
words.zh: 还有一次，他邀请了一些重要的评论家参观他私人收藏的现代绘画。

words.en: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press, for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
words.zh: 这次展览受到了媒体的极大关注，因为虽然这些画被认为是著名艺术家的作品，但实际上它们是迪基画的。

words.en: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
words.zh: 他花了四年时间才上演这个精心设计的笑话，只是为了证明批评者并不总是知道他们在说什么。

words.en: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.
words.zh: 打捞行动彻底失败。

words.en: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.
words.zh: “埃尔科”号小船已经在巴伦支海搜寻了数周，目前正在返航途中。

words.en: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship's captain instructing him to give up the search.
words.zh: 船长收到了来自大陆的无线电消息，指示他放弃搜索。

words.en: The captain knew that another attempt would be made later, for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
words.zh: 船长知道稍后还会进行另一次尝试，因为他要寻找的那艘沉船载着一批珍贵的金条。

words.en: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.
words.zh: 尽管收到了这条消息，埃尔科号的船长还是决定再试一次。

words.en: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
words.zh: 海床被强力的渔网扫过，当一个箱子从海底升起时，船上的人都兴奋不已。

words.en: Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found, the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
words.zh: 尽管船员们一开始以为失落的船已被找到，但箱子里的东西证明他们错了。

words.en: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.
words.zh: 他们实际上发现的是一艘多年前沉没的船。

words.en: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.
words.zh: 箱子里装着海员艾伦·菲尔丁的个人物品。

words.en: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.
words.zh: 里面有书籍、衣服和照片，还有海员曾经从妻子那里收到的信件。

words.en: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
words.zh: 埃尔科号的船长命令他的手下尽可能地从沉船中打捞出更多的东西。

words.en: Nothing of value was found, but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
words.zh: 没有发现任何有价值的东西，但被带到地面的大量物品被证明是非常有趣的。

words.en: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
words.zh: 从举起的一门重炮中，船长意识到这艘船一定是一艘巡洋舰。

words.en: In another chest which contained the belongings of a ship's officer, there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
words.zh: 在另一个装有一名船员物品的箱子里，有一封未完成的信，写于 1943 年 3 月 14 日。

words.en: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.
words.zh: 船长从信中得知，失事的船名为卡伦号。

words.en: The most valuable find of all was the ship's log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.
words.zh: 其中最有价值的发现是该船的航海日志，其中的部分内容仍然可以阅读。

words.en: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.
words.zh: 由此，船长能够拼凑出所有已曝光的信息。

words.en: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.
words.zh: 克伦号在前往俄罗斯的船队中被一艘敌方潜艇鱼雷击中。
