words.en: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.
words.zh: 埃尔科号回国后，国防部的一名海军官员证实了这一点。

words.en: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.
words.zh: 所有发现的物品都被送往战争博物馆。

words.en: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong.
words.zh: 我们都经历过一切都不顺利的日子。

words.en: A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control.
words.zh: 一天的开始可能还不错，但突然间一切似乎都失去了控制。

words.en: What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment.
words.zh: 总是会发生的情况是，很多事情都会在同一时刻选择出错。

words.en: It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions.
words.zh: 就好像一个不重要的事件引发了一系列反应。

words.en: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.
words.zh: 假设您一边准备饭菜，一边照顾宝宝。

words.en: The telephone rings and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes.
words.zh: 电话铃声响起，这标志着一系列不可预见的灾难的前奏。

words.en: While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table, smashing half your best crockery and cutting himself in the process.
words.zh: 当你打电话时，宝宝把桌布从桌子上拉下来，打碎了你最好的陶器的一半，并在这个过程中割伤了自己。

words.en: You hang up hurriedly and attend to baby, crockery, etc.
words.zh: 你匆匆挂断电话，去照顾婴儿、餐具等。

words.en: Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt.
words.zh: 与此同时，饭菜被烧焦了。

words.en: As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner.
words.zh: 似乎这还不足以让你流泪，你的丈夫到来了，出乎意料地带来了三位客人来吃晚饭。

words.en: Things can go wrong on a big scale as a number of people recently discovered in Parramatta, a suburb of Sydney.
words.zh: 正如许多人最近在悉尼郊区帕拉马塔发现的那样，事情可能会出现大规模的问题。

words.en: During the rush hour one evening two cars collided and both drivers began to argue.
words.zh: 一天晚上的高峰时段，两辆车相撞，两名司机开始争吵。

words.en: The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a learner.
words.zh: 紧随两辆车后面的那位女士恰好是一名学习者。

words.en: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.
words.zh: 她突然惊慌失措，把车停了下来。

words.en: This made the driver following her brake hard.
words.zh: 这使得跟随她的司机猛踩刹车。

words.en: His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake.
words.zh: 他的妻子坐在他旁边，手里拿着一个大蛋糕。

words.en: As she was thrown forward, the cake went right through the windscreen and landed on the road.
words.zh: 当她被向前抛时，蛋糕直接穿过挡风玻璃，落在路上。

words.en: Seeing a cake flying through the air, a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
words.zh: 一名停在汽车旁边的卡车司机看到空中飞舞着一块蛋糕，突然把车停了下来。

words.en: The lorry was loaded with empty beer bottles and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and on to the road.
words.zh: 卡车上装满了空啤酒瓶，数百个啤酒瓶从车尾滑落到路上。

words.en: This led to yet another angry argument.
words.zh: 这又引发了另一场愤怒的争论。

words.en: Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind.
words.zh: 与此同时，后面的交通拥堵起来。

words.en: It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again.
words.zh: 警方花了近一个小时才恢复交通。

words.en: In the meantime, the lorry driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles.
words.zh: 与此同时，卡车司机不得不清理数百个破碎的瓶子。

words.en: Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake.
words.zh: 只有两只流浪狗从这一切混乱中受益，因为它们贪婪地吃掉了剩下的蛋糕。

words.en: It was just one of those days!
words.zh: 这只是那些日子之一！

words.en: Antique shops exert a peculiar fascination on a great many people.
words.zh: 古董店对很多人有着独特的吸引力。

words.en: The more expensive kind of antique shop where rare objects are beautifully displayed in glass cases to keep them free from dust is usually a forbidding place.
words.zh: 比较昂贵的古董店通常是一个令人生畏的地方，那里的稀有物品被精美地陈列在玻璃柜中，以防止它们沾染灰尘。

words.en: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.
words.zh: 但没有人必须鼓起勇气才能进入一家不那么自命不凡的古董店。

words.en: There is always hope that in its labyrinth of musty, dark, disordered rooms a real rarity will be found amongst the piles of assorted junk that litter the floors.
words.zh: 人们总是希望，在这个充满霉味、黑暗、杂乱的房间迷宫中，能在地板上乱七八糟的各种垃圾中找到真正的稀有物品。

words.en: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
words.zh: 没有人会偶然发现稀有物品。

words.en: A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience, and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
words.zh: 一个真正专注的讨价还价者必须有耐心，最重要的是，有能力在看到某样东西时认识到它的价值。

words.en: To do this, he must be at least as knowledgeable as the dealer.
words.zh: 要做到这一点，他必须至少和经销商一样知识渊博。

words.en: Like a scientist bent on making a discovery, he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
words.zh: 就像一位致力于做出发现的科学家一样，他必须怀有希望，希望有一天他会得到丰厚的回报。

words.en: My old friend, Frank Halliday, is just such a person.
words.zh: 我的老朋友弗兰克·哈利迪就是这样一个人。

words.en: He has often described to me how he picked up a masterpiece for a mere ￡50.
words.zh: 他经常向我描述他如何仅花费 50 英镑就买到了一幅杰作。

words.en: One Saturday morning, Frank visited an antique shop in my neighbourhood.
words.zh: 一个星期六的早上，弗兰克参观了我家附近的一家古董店。

words.en: As he had never been there before, he found a great deal to interest him.
words.zh: 由于他以前从未去过那里，所以他发现了很多让他感兴趣的东西。

words.en: The morning passed rapidly and Frank was about to leave when he noticed a large packing case lying on the floor.
words.zh: 早上过得很快，弗兰克正要离开，突然发现地板上躺着一个大包装箱。

words.en: The dealer told him that it had just come in, but that he could not be bothered to open it.
words.zh: 经销商告诉他，东西刚到，但他懒得打开。

words.en: Frank begged him to do so and the dealer reluctantly prised it open.
words.zh: 弗兰克恳求他这样做，经销商不情愿地把它打开了。

words.en: The contents were disappointing.
words.zh: 内容令人失望。

words.en: Apart from an interesting-looking carved dagger, the box was full of crockery, much of it broken.
words.zh: 盒子里除了一把看起来很有趣的雕刻匕首外，里面装满了陶器，其中大部分都已经破碎了。

words.en: Frank gently lifted the crockery out of the box and suddenly noticed a miniature painting at the bottom of the packing case.
words.zh: 弗兰克轻轻地将陶器从盒子里拿出来，突然注意到包装箱底部有一幅微型画。

words.en: As its composition and line reminded him of an Italian painting he knew well, he decided to buy it.
words.zh: 由于它的构图和线条让他想起了一幅他熟悉的意大利画作，他决定买下它。

words.en: Glancing at it briefly the dealer told him that it was worth ￡50.
words.zh: 经销商简单地看了一眼，告诉他价值 50 英镑。

words.en: Frank could hardly conceal his excitement, for he knew that he had made a real discovery.
words.zh: 弗兰克难以掩饰自己的兴奋，因为他知道自己有了真正的发现。

words.en: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds and thousands of pounds.
words.zh: 这幅小画被证明是科雷乔的一幅不为人知的杰作，价值数十万英镑。

words.en: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.
words.zh: 正义一词通常与法院联系在一起。

words.en: We might say that justice has been done when a man's innocence or guilt has been proved beyond doubt.
words.zh: 当一个人的清白或有罪被毫无疑问地证明时，我们可以说正义已经得到伸张。

words.en: Justice is part of the complex machinery of the law.
words.zh: 正义是复杂的法律机制的一部分。

words.en: Those who seek it, undertake an arduous journey and can never be sure that they will find it.
words.zh: 那些寻求它的人会经历一段艰辛的旅程，但永远不能确定他们是否会找到它。

words.en: Judges, however wise or eminent, are human and can make mistakes.
words.zh: 法官，无论多么明智或杰出，也是人，也会犯错误。

words.en: There are rare instances when justice almost ceases to be an abstract concept.
words.zh: 在极少数情况下，正义几乎不再是一个抽象概念。

words.en: Reward or punishment are meted out quite independent of human interference.
words.zh: 奖励或惩罚的实施完全独立于人为干预。

words.en: At such times, justice acts like a living force.
words.zh: 在这种时候，正义就像一股活生生的力量。

words.en: When we use a phrase like 'it serves him right', we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
words.zh: 当我们使用“这对他有利”这样的短语时，我们在某种程度上承认，某些特定的情况使正义能够自行行事。

words.en: When a thief was caught on the premises of a large jewellery store one morning, the shop assistants must have found it impossible to resist the temptation to say 'it serves him right'.
words.zh: 一天早上，当一名小偷在一家大型珠宝店内被抓获时，店员一定发现无法抗拒诱惑，说“他活该”。

words.en: The shop was an old converted house with many large, disused fireplaces and tall, narrow chimneys.
words.zh: 这家商店是一栋旧房子改建的，有许多废弃的大壁炉和又高又窄的烟囱。

words.en: Towards midday, a girl heard a muffled cry coming from behind one of the walls.
words.zh: 中午时分，一个女孩听到墙后传来一声低沉的哭声。

words.en: As the cry was repeated several times, she ran to tell the manager who promptly rang up the fire brigade.
words.zh: 由于哭声重复了好几次，她跑去告诉经理，经理立即给消防队打电话。

words.en: The cry had certainly come from one of the chimneys, but as there were so many of them, the firemen could not be certain which one it was.
words.zh: 呼喊声肯定是从其中一个烟囱发出的，但由于烟囱数量太多，消防员无法确定是哪一个。

words.en: They located the right chimney by tapping at the walls and listening for the man's cries.
words.zh: 他们通过敲击墙壁并聆听该男子的哭声找到了正确的烟囱。

words.en: After chipping through a wall which was eighteen inches thick, they found that a man had been trapped in the chimney.
words.zh: 在凿穿十八英寸厚的墙壁后，他们发现一名男子被困在烟囱里。

words.en: As it was extremely narrow, the man was unable to move, but the fire fighters were eventually able to free him by cutting a huge hole in the wall.
words.zh: 由于墙壁极其狭窄，该男子无法移动，但消防队员最终在墙上开了一个大洞，将他救了出来。

words.en: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged, admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
words.zh: 出现的那个脸色黝黑、表情可怜的人立即承认，他曾在夜间试图闯入商店，但被困在烟囱里了。

words.en: He had been there for nearly ten hours.
words.zh: 他已经在那里呆了近十个小时了。

words.en: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.
words.zh: 甚至在该男子被移交给警方之前，正义就已经得到伸张。

courses.title: Lesson 36 · A Chance in a Million

words.en: We are less credulous than we used to be.
words.zh: 我们不像以前那样轻信了。

words.en: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences — most of them wildly improbable.
words.zh: 在十九世纪，小说家会通过向读者呈现一系列巧合来结束他的故事——其中大多数都是极不可能的。

words.en: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
words.zh: 读者们欣然接受了这样一个事实：一个默默无闻的女仆实际上就是主人公的母亲。

words.en: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall.
words.zh: 一个失散多年的兄弟，被认为已经死亡，实际上一直活着，并邪恶地密谋着让英雄垮台。

words.en: And so on.
words.zh: 等等。

words.en: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
words.zh: 现代读者会发现这种幼稚的解决方案完全无法接受。

words.en: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
words.zh: 然而，在现实生活中，环境有时确实会产生巧合，除了十九世纪的小说家之外，任何人都会觉得难以置信。

words.en: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman, found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
words.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我的祖父告诉我，德国出租车司机弗兰茨·巴斯曼如何找到了一个被认为在二十年前被杀的兄弟。

words.en: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
words.zh: 在与妻子徒步旅行时，他停下来与一名工人交谈。

words.en: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband and even suggested that he might be his brother.
words.zh: 他们继续前行后，巴斯曼夫人评论说这名工人与她的丈夫非常相似，甚至暗示他可能是他的兄弟。

words.en: Franz poured scorn on the idea, pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
words.zh: 弗朗茨对这个想法表示蔑视，指出他的兄弟在战争期间阵亡。

words.en: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story, she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
words.zh: 尽管巴斯曼夫人完全熟悉这个故事，但她认为她有百万分之一的可能是对的。

words.en: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
words.zh: 几天后，她派了一个男孩去见那个工人，问他是否叫汉斯·布斯曼。

words.en: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
words.zh: 不用说，这个人的名字叫汉斯·巴斯曼，他确实是弗兰茨失散多年的兄弟。

words.en: When the brothers were reunited, Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
words.zh: 当兄弟俩重聚时，汉斯解释了他为何还活着。

words.en: After having been wounded towards the end of the war, he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
words.zh: 战争快结束时受伤后，他被送往医院并与部队分离。

words.en: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
words.zh: 医院遭到轰炸，汉斯步行返回西德。

words.en: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
words.zh: 与此同时，他的部队失踪了，他的所有记录都被销毁了。

words.en: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
words.zh: 汉斯回到了他的家，但房子被炸了，附近没有人知道居民的情况。

words.en: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid, Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
words.zh: 假设他的家人在空袭中丧生，汉斯在五十英里外的一个村庄定居下来，从那时起他就一直住在那里。

words.en: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
words.zh: 我们已经学会期待火车准点。

words.en: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
words.zh: 经过多年的磨练，我们大多数人都对铁路时刻表产生了不可动摇的信心。

words.en: Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
words.zh: 船舶可能因暴风雨而延误；航班可能因恶劣天气而取消；但火车必须准时。

words.en: Only an exceptionally heavy snow fall might temporarily dislocate railway services.
words.zh: 只有特大雪可能会暂时扰乱铁路服务。

words.en: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
words.zh: 当出现问题时，人们很容易责怪铁路当局。

words.en: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.
words.zh: 事实是，当错误发生时，错误更有可能是我们的，而不是他们的。

words.en: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.
words.zh: 查阅了火车时刻表后，我满意地注意到有一趟开往韦斯特黑文的特快列车。

words.en: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.
words.zh: 它从我当地的车站直达，旅程仅持续了一个小时十七分钟。

words.en: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
words.zh: 当我登上火车时，我不禁注意到车上也有很多当地人。

words.en: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.
words.zh: 当时，这并不让我感到奇怪。

words.en: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
words.zh: 我想，除了我之外，肯定还有很多人想要享受这项优质的服务。

words.en: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
words.zh: 当火车停在威德利车站时，我也不感到惊讶，威德利车站是沿线几英里的一个小车站。

words.en: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
words.zh: 即使是强大的特快列车也能被信号灯阻挡。

words.en: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder.
words.zh: 但当火车在一个又一个车站磨蹭时，我开始怀疑。

words.en: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
words.zh: 我突然意识到，这趟快车并不是以每小时九十英里的速度呼啸而过，而是以三十英里的速度勉强行驶。

words.en: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.
words.zh: 一小时十七分钟过去了，我们还没有走完一半的路程。

words.en: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.
words.zh: 我问一位乘客这是不是Westhaven Express，但他根本没有听说过。

words.en: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.
words.zh: 我决定一到达就提出投诉。

words.en: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.
words.zh: 两个小时后，我愤怒地跟西港站长说话。

words.en: When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.
words.zh: 当他否认火车的存在时，我借了他的时刻表副本。

words.en: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
words.zh: 当我告诉他这本书是白纸黑字的时候，我的声音里充满了胜利的气息。

words.en: Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again.
words.zh: 他简单地看了一眼，让我再看一遍。

words.en: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.
words.zh: 一个小星号引导我到页面底部的脚注。

words.en: It said: 'This service has been suspended.'
words.zh: 它说：“这项服务已暂停。”

words.en: Future historians will be in a unique position when they come to record the history of our own times.
words.zh: 未来的历史学家在记录我们这个时代的历史时将处于独特的地位。

words.en: They will hardly know which facts to select from the great mass of evidence that steadily accumulates.
words.zh: 他们几乎不知道该从不断积累的大量证据中选择哪些事实。

words.en: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.
words.zh: 更重要的是，他们不必仅仅依赖书面文字。

words.en: Films, videos, CDs and CD-ROMs are just some of the bewildering amount of information they will have.
words.zh: 电影、视频、CD 和 CD-ROM 只是它们所拥有的海量信息中的一部分。

words.en: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.
words.zh: 可以说，他们将能够看到和听到我们的行动。

words.en: But the historian attempting to reconstruct the distant past is always faced with a difficult task.
words.zh: 但试图重建遥远过去的历史学家总是面临着艰巨的任务。

words.en: He has to deduce what he can from the few scanty clues available.
words.zh: 他必须从仅有的少量线索中推断出他能得出的结论。

words.en: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
words.zh: 即使是看似微不足道的遗迹也可以为早期人类的历史提供有趣的线索。

words.en: Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture, for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
words.zh: 到目前为止，历史学家一直认为日历是随着农业的出现而出现的，因为那时人类面临着了解季节的真正需要。

words.en: Recent scientific evidence seems to indicate that this assumption is incorrect.
words.zh: 最近的科学证据似乎表明这种假设是不正确的。

words.en: Historians have long been puzzled by dots, lines and symbols which have been engraved on walls, bones, and the ivory tusks of mammoths.
words.zh: 长期以来，历史学家一直对刻在墙壁、骨头和猛犸象象牙上的点、线和符号感到困惑。

words.en: The nomads who made these markings lived by hunting and fishing during the last Ice Age which began about 35,000 B.C. and ended about 10,000 B.C. By correlating markings made in various parts of the world, historians have been able to read this difficult code.
words.zh: 在大约公元前 35,000 年开始的最后一个冰河时期，留下这些标记的游牧民族以狩猎和捕鱼为生。并于公元前 10,000 年左右结束。通过关联世界各地的标记，历史学家已经能够解读这段困难的代码。

words.en: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.
words.zh: 他们发现它与日子的流逝和月相有关。

words.en: It is, in fact, a primitive type of calendar.
words.zh: 事实上，它是一种原始类型的日历。

words.en: It has long been known that the hunting scenes depicted on walls were not simply a form of artistic expression.
words.zh: 人们早就知道，墙上描绘的狩猎场景不仅仅是一种艺术表现形式。

words.en: They had a definite meaning, for they were as near as early man could get to writing.
words.zh: 它们具有明确的意义，因为它们是早期人类能够书写的最接近的东西。

words.en: It is possible that there is a definite relation between these paintings and the markings that sometimes accompany them.
words.zh: 这些画作和有时伴随它们的标记之间可能存在明确的关系。

words.en: It seems that man was making a real effort to understand the seasons 20,000 years earlier than has been supposed.
words.zh: 人类似乎正在付出真正的努力来理解季节，比人们想象的要早两万年。

words.en: The rough road across the plain soon became so bad that we tried to get Bruce to drive back to the village we had come from.
words.zh: 穿过平原的崎岖道路很快就变得非常糟糕，我们试图让布鲁斯开车回到我们原来的村庄。

words.en: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.
words.zh: 尽管路上布满了巨石，坑坑洼洼，布鲁斯却没有丝毫不安。

words.en: Glancing at his map, he informed us that the next village was a mere twenty miles away.
words.zh: 他看了一眼地图，告诉我们下一个村庄距离我们只有二十英里。

words.en: It was not that Bruce always underestimated difficulties.
words.zh: 布鲁斯并不是总是低估困难。

words.en: He simply had no sense of danger at all.
words.zh: 他根本就没有任何危险的感觉。

words.en: No matter what the conditions were, he believed that a car should be driven as fast as it could possibly go.
words.zh: 无论条件如何，他相信汽车应该开得尽可能快。

words.en: As we bumped over the dusty track, we swerved to avoid large boulders.
words.zh: 当我们在尘土飞扬的轨道上颠簸时，我们突然转向以避免大石块。

words.en: The wheels scooped up stones which hammered ominously under the car.
words.zh: 车轮卷起石头，不祥地敲击着车底。

words.en: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.
words.zh: 我们确信，一块石头迟早会在我们的油箱上划出一个洞，或者损坏发动机。

words.en: Because of this, we kept looking back, wondering if we were leaving a trail of oil and petrol behind us.
words.zh: 正因为如此，我们不断回头，想知道我们身后是否留下了石油和汽油的踪迹。

words.en: What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared, giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps bushes.
words.zh: 当巨石突然消失，取而代之的是一片平原时，唯一的障碍就是灌木丛，这真是一种解脱。

words.en: But there was worse to come.
words.zh: 但更糟糕的事情还在后面。

words.en: Just ahead of us there was a huge fissure.
words.zh: 就在我们前方，出现了一条巨大的裂缝。

words.en: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.
words.zh: 为了回应新的恳求，布鲁斯停了下来。

words.en: Though we all got out to examine the fissure, he remained in the car.
words.zh: 尽管我们都下车检查裂缝，但他仍然留在车里。

words.en: We informed him that the fissure extended for fifty yards and was two feet wide and four feet deep.
words.zh: 我们告诉他，裂缝延伸了五十码，宽两英尺，深四英尺。

words.en: Even this had no effect.
words.zh: 即使这样也没有效果。

words.en: Bruce went into a low gear and drove at a terrifying speed, keeping the front wheels astride the crack as he followed its zigzag course.
words.zh: 布鲁斯挂入低速档，以可怕的速度行驶，在沿着锯齿状路线行驶时，前轮跨过裂缝。

words.en: Before we had time to worry about what might happen, we were back on the plain again.
words.zh: 还没来得及担心会发生什么，我们又回到了平原。

words.en: Bruce consulted the map once more and told us that the village was now only fifteen miles away.
words.zh: 布鲁斯再次查阅了地图，告诉我们现在距离村庄只有十五英里了。

words.en: Our next obstacle was a shallow pool of water about half a mile across.
words.zh: 我们的下一个障碍是一个大约半英里宽的浅水池。

words.en: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.
words.zh: 布鲁斯冲向它，但在半途中，汽车嘎然而止。

words.en: A yellow light on the dashboard flashed angrily and Bruce cheerfully announced that there was no oil in the engine!
words.zh: 仪表板上的黄灯愤怒地闪烁，布鲁斯高兴地宣布发动机没油了！

words.en: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.
words.zh: 从来没有人解释过为什么大学生似乎比其他人更喜欢恶作剧。

words.en: Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax.
words.zh: 学生们专门研究一种特殊类型的恶作剧：恶作剧。

words.en: Inviting the fire brigade to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception which no self-respecting student would ever indulde in.
words.zh: 邀请消防队去扑灭一场不存在的火灾是一种粗俗的欺骗行为，任何有自尊心的学生都不会这么做。

words.en: Students often create amusing situations which are funny to everyone except the victims.
words.zh: 学生们经常创造一些有趣的场景，除了受害者之外，每个人都觉得有趣。

words.en: When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university, he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
words.zh: 近日，一名学生在大学外看到两名工人在使用风钻，他立即打电话报警，告知警方有两名学生打扮成工人，正在用风钻撕毁道路。

words.en: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away, they were not to take him seriously.
words.zh: 挂断电话后，他走到工人们面前，告诉他们，如果警察命令他们走开，他们就不要把他当回事。

words.en: He added that a student had dressed up as a policeman and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people.
words.zh: 他补充说，一名学生打扮成警察，向人们开各种愚蠢的玩笑。

words.en: Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information.
words.zh: 警察和工人都对学生提前提供的信息表示感谢。

words.en: The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on.
words.zh: 这名学生躲在附近的一个拱门里，在那里他可以看到并听到发生的一切。

words.en: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.
words.zh: 果不其然，一名警察赶到了现场，礼貌地请工人离开。

words.en: When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he threatened to remove them by force.
words.zh: 当他收到一名工人非常粗鲁的答复时，他威胁要用武力驱逐他们。

words.en: The workmen told him to do as he pleased and the policeman telephoned for help.
words.zh: 工人们让他随心所欲，警察打电话寻求帮助。

words.en: Shortly afterwards, 4 more policemen arrived and remonstrated with the workmen.
words.zh: 不久之后，又有4名警察赶到，对工人进行抗议。

words.en: As the men refused to stop working, the police attempted to seize the pneumatic drill.
words.zh: 由于这些人拒绝停止工作，警察试图没收风钻。

words.en: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.
words.zh: 工人们激烈挣扎，其中一人发脾气。

words.en: He threatened to call the police.
words.zh: 他威胁要报警。

words.en: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.
words.zh: 对此，警方讽刺地指出，这几乎没有必要，因为这些人已经被捕。

words.en: Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station.
words.zh: 一名工人假装严肃地询问他是否可以在被带到车站之前打个电话。

words.en: Permission was granted and a policeman accompanied him to a pay phone.
words.zh: 获得许可后，一名警察陪同他前往公用电话。

words.en: Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did he realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.
words.zh: 当他看到那人居然给警察打电话时，他才意识到他们都是骗局的受害者。

words.en: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
words.zh: 乡村的平静生活从来没有吸引过我。

words.en: City born and city bred, I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasionally visit during the weekend.
words.zh: 我出生在城市，长在城市，一直把乡村视为透过火车车窗看到的东西，或者周末偶尔去的地方。

words.en: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
words.zh: 我的大多数朋友都生活在城市里，但一提到乡村，他们总是欣喜若狂。

words.en: Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life, only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
words.zh: 尽管他们颂扬和平生活的美德，但他们中只有一个人曾经去乡下生活过，并且在六个月内就回到了城里。

words.en: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
words.zh: 甚至他仍然生活在乡村生活比城镇生活优越的幻想之中。

words.en: He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
words.zh: 他总是在谈论友好的人民、干净的气氛、亲近自然和温和的生活节奏。

words.en: Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn, the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
words.zh: 他坚持认为，没有什么可以与第一声公鸡报晓、黎明时鸟儿的叽叽喳喳声、初升的太阳在树木和牧场上闪闪发光的景象相比。

words.en: This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.
words.zh: 这田园诗般的田园风光只是图片的一部分。

words.en: My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV — virtually the only form of entertainment.
words.zh: 我的朋友没有提到电视前漫长而没有朋友的冬夜——这几乎是唯一的娱乐形式。

words.en: He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops, or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
words.zh: 他只字未提商店里商品的选择不佳，也没有提及那些每天必须从乡村到城市上班的不幸的人。

words.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
words.zh: 我无法理解为什么人们愿意忍受每天四个小时的旅行，以换取在乡村生活的可疑特权。

words.en: They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.
words.zh: 如果他们选择生活在他们真正所属的城市，他们可以节省很多痛苦和费用。

words.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
words.zh: 如果您可以远离乡村的一些田园风光，您会发现城市可以为您提供生活所能提供的最好的东西。

words.en: You never have to travel miles to see your friends.
words.zh: 您无需长途跋涉就能见到您的朋友。

words.en: They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening's entertainment.
words.zh: 他们总是住在附近，随时可以进行非正式的聊天或晚上的娱乐活动。

words.en: Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.
words.zh: 我在乡下的一些熟人每年都会来城里一两次参观剧院，作为一种特殊的享受。

words.en: For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.
words.zh: 对于他们来说，这是一项涉及大量计划的重大行动。

words.en: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
words.zh: 随着演出接近尾声，他们想知道是否能赶上最后一班火车回家。

words.en: The city dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.
words.zh: 城市居民从来没有经历过这种焦虑。

words.en: The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
words.zh: 最新的展览、电影或戏剧距离酒店仅有很短的巴士车程。

words.en: Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
words.zh: 购物也总是一种乐趣。

words.en: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
words.zh: 种类繁多，您永远不必屈居第二。

words.en: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.
words.zh: 乡下人在城里购物时会疯狂，然后带着尽可能多的异国情调物品摇摇晃晃地回家。

words.en: Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.
words.zh: 这座城市也并非没有美丽的时刻。

words.en: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
words.zh: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜，广告发出的温暖光芒让人感到安慰。

words.en: Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
words.zh: 没有什么比周末空荡荡的城市街道上的宁静更令人印象深刻的了，每天上班的数千人都躲在乡下的家中。

words.en: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers, who appreciate all these things, obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.
words.zh: 对我来说，一直有一个不解之谜：为什么欣赏这一切的城市居民却固执地假装他们更喜欢住在乡村。

words.en: Cave exploration, or pot-holing, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport.
words.zh: 洞穴探险，或众所周知的洞穴探险，是一项相对较新的运动。

words.en: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.
words.zh: 也许是对孤独的渴望，或者是有意外发现的机会，吸引着人们来到地球深处。

words.en: It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a pot-holer's motives.
words.zh: 对于挖洞者的动机不可能给出令人满意的解释。

words.en: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
words.zh: 对他来说，洞穴有着与高山对登山者同样的独特魅力。

words.en: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.
words.zh: 它们唤起人们只能隐约理解的本能。

words.en: Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler.
words.zh: 对于周日下午的漫步者来说，探索非常深的洞穴并不是一项任务。

words.en: Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of military operations.
words.zh: 这些任务需要军事行动的精确规划和远见。

words.en: It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and to establish supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave.
words.zh: 在下降到一个非常深的洞穴之前，可能需要长达八天的时间来安装绳梯并建立补给基地。

words.en: Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties which will confront the pot-holer.
words.zh: 这种预防措施是必要的，因为不可能预测挖洞者将面临的困难的确切性质。

words.en: The deepest known cave in the world is the Gouffre Berger near Grenoble.
words.zh: 世界上已知最深的洞穴是格勒诺布尔附近的古弗尔伯格洞穴。

words.en: It extends to a depth of 3,723 feet.
words.zh: 它延伸至 3,723 英尺的深度。

words.en: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunnelled a course through a flaw in the rocks.
words.zh: 这个巨大的裂缝是由一条地下溪流穿过岩石的裂缝形成的。

words.en: The entrance to the cave is on a plateau in the Dauphine Alps.
words.zh: 洞穴的入口位于多芬阿尔卑斯山的一个高原上。

words.en: As it is only six feet across, it is barely noticeable.
words.zh: 因为它只有六英尺宽，所以很难被注意到。

words.en: The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.
words.zh: 如果不是杰出的法国坑洞专家伯杰发现了入口，这个洞穴可能永远不会被发现。

words.en: Since its discovery, it has become a sort of pot-holers' Everest.
words.zh: 自被发现以来，它已成为洞穴探险者的珠穆朗玛峰。

words.en: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.
words.zh: 尽管已经进行了多次下降，但其中大部分仍有待探索。

words.en: A team of pot-holers recently went down the Gouffre Berger.
words.zh: 最近，一队坑洞探险者沿着古弗尔伯杰 (Gouffre Berger) 探险。

words.en: After entering the narrow gap on the plateau, they climbed down the steep sides of the cave until they came to a narrow corridor.
words.zh: 进入高原上的狭窄缝隙后，他们顺着陡峭的山洞往下爬，直到来到一条狭窄的甬道前。

words.en: They had to edge their way along this, sometimes wading across shallow streams, or swimming across deep pools.
words.zh: 他们必须沿着这条路慢慢前行，有时涉过浅溪，或游过深潭。

words.en: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.
words.zh: 突然，他们来到了一个瀑布，瀑布落入洞底的地下湖中。

words.en: They plunged into the lake, and after loading their gear on an inflatable rubber dinghy, let the current carry them to the other side.
words.zh: 他们跳入湖中，将装备装上充气橡皮艇后，让水流将他们带到对岸。

words.en: To protect themselves from the icy water, they had to wear special rubber suits.
words.zh: 为了保护自己免受冰冷的水的伤害，他们必须穿上特殊的橡胶服。

words.en: At the far end of the lake, they came to huge piles of rubble which had been washed up by the water.
words.zh: 到了湖的尽头，他们来到了被水冲刷的巨大瓦砾堆前。

words.en: In this part of the cave, they could hear an insistent booming sound which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down into a pool from the roof of the cave.
words.zh: 在洞穴的这一部分，他们可以听到持续不断的轰鸣声，他们发现这是由一个小水龙卷从洞穴顶部喷入水池引起的。

words.en: Squeezing through a cleft in the rocks, the pot-holers arrived at an enormous cavern, the size of a huge concert hall.
words.zh: 钻洞者们挤过岩石裂缝，到达了一个巨大的洞穴，其大小相当于一个巨大的音乐厅。

words.en: After switching on powerful arc lights, they saw great stalagmites — some of them over forty feet high — rising up like tree-trunks to meet the stalactites suspended from the roof.
words.zh: 打开强大的弧光灯后，他们看到巨大的石笋——其中一些超过四十英尺高——像树干一样升起，与悬挂在屋顶上的钟乳石相遇。

words.en: Round about, piles of limestone glistened in all the colours of the rainbow.
words.zh: 周围，​​成堆的石灰石闪烁着彩虹般的色彩。

words.en: In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound that could be heard was made by water which dripped continuously from the high dome above them.
words.zh: 山洞里一片诡异的寂静，唯一能听到的声音就是从头顶高高的穹顶上不断滴下的水声。

words.en: Insurance companies are normally willing to insure anything.
words.zh: 保险公司通常愿意为任何事情提供保险。

words.en: Insuring public or private property is a standard practice in most countries in the world.
words.zh: 为公共或私人财产提供保险是世界上大多数国家的标准做法。

words.en: If, however, you were holding an open air garden party or a fete it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
words.zh: 然而，如果您要举办露天花园派对或宴会，同样可以在恶劣天气的情况下为自己投保。

words.en: Needless to say, the bigger the risk an insurance company takes, the higher the premium you will have to pay.
words.zh: 不用说，保险公司承担的风险越大，您需要支付的保费就越高。

words.en: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the cost of salvaging a sunken ship.
words.zh: 航运公司对打捞沉船的费用提出索赔的情况并不罕见。

words.en: But the claim made by a local authority to recover the cost of salvaging a sunken pie dish must surely be unique.
words.zh: 但地方当局声称要收回打捞沉没馅饼盘的费用，这肯定是独一无二的。

words.en: Admittedly it was an unusual pie dish, for it was eighteen feet long and six feet wide.
words.zh: 诚然，这是一个不寻常的馅饼盘，因为它长十八英尺，宽六英尺。

words.en: It had been purchased by a local authority so that an enormous pie could be baked for an annual fair.
words.zh: 它被当地政府购买，以便为一年一度的集市烤制一个巨大的馅饼。

words.en: The pie committee decided that the best way to transport the dish would be by canal so they insured it for the trip.
words.zh: 馅饼委员会决定运输这道菜的最佳方式是通过运河，因此他们为这次旅行投了保险。

words.en: Shortly after it was launched, the pie committee went to a local inn to celebrate.
words.zh: 上线后不久，馅饼委员会就前往当地一家旅馆庆祝。

words.en: At the same time, a number of teenagers climbed on to the dish and held a little party of their own.
words.zh: 与此同时，一些青少年爬上盘子，举办了一场他们自己的小型聚会。

words.en: Dancing proved to be more than the dish could bear, for during the party it capsized and sank in seven feet of water.
words.zh: 事实证明，跳舞超出了盘子的承受能力，因为在聚会期间它翻了，沉入了七英尺深的水中。

words.en: The pie committee telephoned a local garage owner who arrived in a recovery truck to salvage the pie dish.
words.zh: 馅饼委员会给当地一位车库老板打电话，后者开着一辆回收卡车来抢救馅饼盘。

words.en: Shivering in their wet clothes, the teenagers looked on while three men dived repeatedly into the water to locate the dish.
words.zh: 青少年们穿着湿衣服瑟瑟发抖，他们在一旁看着，三名男子不断潜入水中寻找盘子。

words.en: They had little difficulty in finding it, but hauling it out of the water proved to be a serious problem.
words.zh: 他们很容易找到它，但把它从水中拖出来却是一个严重的问题。

words.en: The sides of the dish were so smooth that it was almost impossible to attach hawsers and chains to the rim without damaging it.
words.zh: 盘子的侧面非常光滑，几乎不可能将缆索和链条连接到边缘而不损坏它。

words.en: Eventually chains were fixed to one end of the dish and a powerful winch was put into operation.
words.zh: 最终，链条被固定在盘的一端，一台强大的绞盘投入运行。

words.en: The dish rose to the surface and was gently drawn towards the canal bank.
words.zh: 盘子升到水面并被轻轻地拉向运河岸边。

words.en: For one agonizing moment, the dish was perched precariously on the bank of the canal, but it suddenly overbalanced and slid back into the water.
words.zh: 在令人痛苦的时刻，盘子摇摇欲坠地停在运河岸边，但它突然失去平衡并滑回水中。

words.en: The men were now obliged to try once more.
words.zh: 这些人现在不得不再试一次。

words.en: This time they fixed heavy metal clamps to both sides of the dish so that they could fasten the chains.
words.zh: 这次，他们在盘子的两侧固定了沉重的金属夹，以便固定链条。

words.en: The dish now had to be lifted vertically because one edge was resting against the side of the canal.
words.zh: 现在必须垂直抬起盘子，因为它的一个边缘靠在运河的一侧。

words.en: The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
words.zh: 绞车再次投入使用，其中一名男子启动了卡车。

words.en: Several minutes later, the dish was successfully hauled above the surface of the water.
words.zh: 几分钟后，盘子被成功拖出水面。

words.en: Water streamed in torrents over its sides with such force that it set up a huge wave in the canal.
words.zh: 水流从它的两侧汹涌而过，力量如此之大，在运河中掀起了巨大的波浪。

words.en: There was a danger that the wave would rebound off the other side of the bank and send the dish plunging into the water again.
words.zh: 存在这样的危险：波浪会从河岸的另一边反弹，使盘子再次落入水中。

words.en: By working at tremendous speed, the men managed to get the dish on to dry land before the wave returned.
words.zh: 通过以极快的速度工作，人们成功地在海浪回来之前将盘子放到了干燥的陆地上。

words.en: People travelling long distances frequently have to decide whether they would prefer to go by land, sea, or air.
words.zh: 长途旅行的人们经常需要决定是选择陆路、海运还是空运。

words.en: Hardly anyone can positively enjoy sitting in a train for more than a few hours.
words.zh: 几乎没有人能真正享受在火车上坐几个小时以上的乐趣。

words.en: Train compartments soon get cramped and stuffy.
words.zh: 火车车厢很快就会变得狭窄和闷热。

words.en: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
words.zh: 几乎不可能让你的注意力从旅途中移开。

words.en: Reading is only a partial solution, for the monotonous rhythm of the wheels clicking on the rails soon lull you to sleep.
words.zh: 阅读只是部分解决方案，因为轮子敲击铁轨的单调节奏很快就会让你入睡。

words.en: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.
words.zh: 白天，睡眠断断续续。

words.en: At night, when you really wish to go to sleep, you rarely manage to do so.
words.zh: 晚上，当你真的想睡觉时，你很少能睡着。

words.en: If you are lucky enough to get a sleeper, you spend half the night staring at the small blue light in the ceiling, or fumbling to find your ticket for inspection.
words.zh: 如果你足够幸运，能买到卧铺车，你会花半个晚上的时间盯着天花板上的小蓝灯，或者摸索着寻找你的票以供检查。

words.en: Inevitably you arrive at your destination almost exhausted.
words.zh: 不可避免地，您到达目的地时几乎精疲力尽。

words.en: Long car journeys are even less pleasant, for it is quite impossible even to read.
words.zh: 长途汽车旅行更不愉快，因为连读书都是不可能的。

words.en: On motorways you can, at least, travel fairly safely at high speeds, but more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on roads with few service stations and too much traffic.
words.zh: 在高速公路上，您至少可以相当安全地高速行驶，但通常情况下，大部分行程都花在服务站很少且交通拥堵的道路上。

words.en: By comparison, ferry trips or cruises offer a great variety of civilized comforts.
words.zh: 相比之下，渡轮旅行或游轮提供了多种文明的舒适体验。

words.en: You can stretch your legs on the spacious decks, play games, meet interesting people and enjoy good food — always assuming, of course, that the sea is calm.
words.zh: 您可以在宽敞的甲板上伸展双腿、玩游戏、结识有趣的人并享受美食——当然，前提是海面是平静的。

words.en: If it is not, and you are likely to get seasick, no form of transport could be worse.
words.zh: 如果不是，您可能会晕船，没有比这更糟糕的交通方式了。

words.en: Even if you travel in ideal weather, sea journeys take a long time.
words.zh: 即使您在理想的天气下旅行，海上旅行也需要很长时间。

words.en: Relatively few people are prepared to sacrifice holiday time for the pleasure of travelling by sea.
words.zh: 相对较少的人愿意牺牲假期时间来享受海上旅行的乐趣。

words.en: Aeroplanes have the reputation of being dangerous and even hardened travellers are intimidated by them.
words.zh: 飞机因危险而闻名，即使是经验丰富的旅行者也会被它们吓倒。

words.en: They also have the disadvantage of being an expensive form of transport.
words.zh: 它们还具有作为一种昂贵的运输方式的缺点。

words.en: But nothing can match them for speed and comfort.
words.zh: 但在速度和舒适度方面没有什么可以与它们相比。

words.en: Travelling at a height of 30,000 feet, far above the clouds, and at over 500 miles an hour is an exhilarating experience.
words.zh: 在 30,000 英尺的高度、远在云层之上、以超过每小时 500 英里的速度旅行是一种令人兴奋的体验。

words.en: You do not have to devise ways of taking your mind off the journey, for an aeroplane gets you to your destination rapidly.
words.zh: 您无需想办法让自己的注意力从旅途中转移开，因为飞机可以快速将您送达目的地。

words.en: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.
words.zh: 在接下来的几个小时里，您可以靠在一张很深的扶手椅上享受飞行的乐趣。

words.en: The real escapist can watch a film and sip champagne on some services.
words.zh: 真正想暂时摆脱现实的人，在某些航班上还可以边看电影边喝香槟。

words.en: But even when such refinements are not available, there is plenty to keep you occupied.
words.zh: 但即使无法进行此类改进，也有很多事情可以让您忙碌。

words.en: An aeroplane offers you an unusual and breathtaking view of the world.
words.zh: 飞机为您提供不寻常且令人惊叹的世界景观。

words.en: You soar effortlessly over high mountains and deep valleys.
words.zh: 你毫不费力地飞过高山和深谷。

words.en: You really see the shape of the land.
words.zh: 你确实看到了土地的形状。

words.en: If the landscape is hidden from view, you can enjoy the extraordinary sight of unbroken cloud plains that stretch out for miles before you, while the sun shines brilliantly in a clear sky.
words.zh: 如果风景看不见，您可以欣赏到在您面前绵延数英里的连绵云平原的非凡景象，同时阳光在晴朗的天空中闪耀。

words.en: The journey is so smooth that there is nothing to prevent you from reading or sleeping.
words.zh: 旅途非常顺利，没有什么可以妨碍你读书或睡觉。

words.en: However you decide to spend your time, one thing is certain: you will arrive at your destination fresh and uncrumpled.
words.zh: 无论您决定如何度过时间，有一点是确定的：您将精神饱满地抵达目的地。

words.en: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.
words.zh: 您不必在接下来的几天里从漫长而艰辛的旅程中恢复过来。

courses.title: Lesson 45 · The Power of the Press

words.en: In democratic countries any efforts to restrict the freedom of the press are rightly condemned.
words.zh: 在民主国家，任何限制新闻自由的行为都会受到正确的谴责。

words.en: However, this freedom can easily be abused.
words.zh: 然而，这种自由很容易被滥用。

words.en: Stories about people often attract far more public attention than political events.
words.zh: 关于人物的故事往往比政治事件更能吸引公众的关注。

words.en: Though we may enjoy reading about the lives of others, it is extremely doubtful whether we would equally enjoy reading about ourselves.
words.zh: 尽管我们可能喜欢阅读别人的生活，但我们是否也同样喜欢阅读自己的生活是非常值得怀疑的。

words.en: Acting on the contention that facts are sacred, reporters can cause untold suffering to individuals by publishing details about their private lives.
words.zh: 记者秉持事实神圣不可侵犯的论点，通过发布有关个人私生活的细节，可能会给个人带来难以言表的痛苦。

words.en: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people but can even overthrow a government.
words.zh: 报纸的影响力如此之大，不仅可以给普通民众的生活带来重大改变，甚至可以推翻一个政府。

words.en: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight, dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
words.zh: 一个贫困家庭一夜名声大噪的故事，生动地说明了媒体的力量。

words.en: The family lived in Aberdeen, a small town of 23,000 inhabitants in South Dakota.
words.zh: 这家人住在南达科他州一个拥有 23,000 名居民的小镇阿伯丁。

words.en: As the parents had five children, life was a perpetual struggle against poverty.
words.zh: 由于父母有五个孩子，生活就是与贫困的永久斗争。

words.en: They were expecting their sixth child and were faced with even more pressing economic problems.
words.zh: 他们即将迎来第六个孩子，并面临着更加紧迫的经济问题。

words.en: If they had only had one more child, the fact would have passed unnoticed.
words.zh: 如果他们再多生一个孩子，这一事实就会被忽视。

words.en: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds and would have lived in obscurity.
words.zh: 他们将继续与经济困难作斗争，并默默无闻地生活。

words.en: But they suddenly became the parents of quintuplets, four girls and a boy, an event which radically changed their lives.
words.zh: 但他们突然成为五胞胎的父母，四个女孩和一个男孩，这一事件彻底改变了他们的生活。

words.en: The day after the birth of the five children, an aeroplane arrived in Aberdeen bringing sixty reporters and photographers.
words.zh: 五个孩子出生的第二天，一架载着六十名记者和摄影师的飞机抵达阿伯丁。

words.en: The rise to fame was swift.
words.zh: 成名的速度很快。

words.en: Television cameras and newspapers carried the news to everyone in the country.
words.zh: 电视摄像机和报纸将这一消息传播给全国每个人。

words.en: Newspapers and magazines offered the family huge sums for the exclusive rights to publish stories and photographs.
words.zh: 报纸和杂志为这个家族提供了巨额报酬，以获得发表故事和照片的独家权利。

words.en: Gifts poured in not only from unknown people, but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
words.zh: 礼物不仅来自不知名的人，还来自希望为其产品做广告的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。

words.en: The old farmhouse the family lived in was to be replaced by a new $500,000 home.
words.zh: 他们一家人居住的旧农舍将被一座价值 50 万美元的新房子取代。

words.en: Reporters kept pressing for interviews so lawyers had to be employed to act as spokesmen for the family at press conferences.
words.zh: 记者不断催促采访，因此不得不聘请律师在新闻发布会上担任家属的发言人。

words.en: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery, their parents were paying the price for fame.
words.zh: 当这五个婴儿仍然安静地睡在医院托儿所的氧气帐篷里时，他们的父母正在为名誉付出代价。

words.en: It would never again be possible for them to lead normal lives.
words.zh: 他们再也不可能过上正常的生活了。

words.en: They had become the victims of commercialization, for their names had acquired a market value.
words.zh: 他们已经成为商业化的受害者，因为他们的名字已经获得了市场价值。

words.en: Instead of being five new family members, these children had immediately become a commodity.
words.zh: 这些孩子不再是五个新的家庭成员，而是立即成为一种商品。

words.en: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves, that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
words.zh: 我们对自己做事的热情是如此之大，以至于我们对专业劳动力的依赖越来越少。

words.en: No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer, for there are countless do-it-yourself publications.
words.zh: 没有人可以再以对某个主题的无知为借口，因为有无数的自己动手的出版物。

words.en: Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
words.zh: 有了合适的工具和材料，新婚夫妇就可以愉快地开始装饰自己的家了。

words.en: Men, particularly, spend hours of their leisure time installing their own fireplaces, laying out their own gardens; building garages and making furniture.
words.zh: 尤其是男人，他们会花几个小时的闲暇时间安装自己的壁炉，布置自己的花园；建造车库和制作家具。

words.en: Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
words.zh: 一些真正热心的爱好者甚至建造了自己的计算机。

words.en: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices, but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
words.zh: 商店为了迎合DIY热潮，不仅为新手提供特别咨询服务，还为消费者提供可以在家组装的零配件。

words.en: Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent up creative energy, but unfortunately not all of us are born handymen.
words.zh: 这些东西为被压抑的创造力提供了一个极好的出口，但不幸的是，并不是我们所有人都是天生的勤杂工。

words.en: Some wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and can fix anything.
words.zh: 有些妻子倾向于相信她们的丈夫足智多谋，可以解决任何问题。

words.en: Even men who can hardly drive a nail in straight are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers and mechanics.
words.zh: 即使是连钉子都钉不直的人也应该是天生的电工、木匠、水管工和机械师。

words.en: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate, some women assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
words.zh: 当电灯熔断、家具摇摇晃晃、管道堵塞或吸尘器无法工作时，一些女性认为她们的丈夫会以某种方式纠正事情。

words.en: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything, even when they have repeatedly been proved wrong.
words.zh: 自己动手游戏最糟糕的是，有时甚至男人也生活在自己可以做任何事情的错觉中，即使他们一再被证明是错误的。

words.en: It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
words.zh: 这与其他任何事情一样都是一个骄傲问题。

words.en: Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
words.zh: 去年春天，我妻子建议我叫一个男人来看看我们的割草机。

words.en: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
words.zh: 去年夏天它坏了，虽然我答应修理它，但我一直没有时间去做。

words.en: I would not hear of the suggestion and said that I would fix it myself.
words.zh: 我不听这个建议，并说我会自己解决。

words.en: One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden and had a close look at it.
words.zh: 一个星期六的下午，我把机器拖到花园里仔细观察。

words.en: As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
words.zh: 据我所知，它只需要一个小小的调整：这里拧一下螺丝，那里拧紧一点，滴一滴油，它就会像新的一样。

words.en: Inevitably the repair job was not quite so simple.
words.zh: 不可避免的是，修复工作并不那么简单。

words.en: The mower firmly refused to mow, so I decided to dismantle it.
words.zh: 割草机坚决不肯割草，所以我决定把它拆掉。

words.en: The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.
words.zh: 花园里很快就堆满了曾经用来制作割草机的金属块。

words.en: But I was extremely pleased with myself.
words.zh: 但我对自己感到非常满意。

words.en: I had traced the cause of the trouble.
words.zh: 我已经查明了问题的原因。

words.en: One of the links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
words.zh: 驱动车轮的链条中的一个环节断裂了。

words.en: After buying a new chain I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.
words.zh: 购买新链条后，我面临着将令人困惑的拼图游戏重新拼凑起来的艰巨任务。

words.en: I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it, for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal which did not seem to fit anywhere.
words.zh: 我毫不惊讶地发现，在我重新组装机器后，机器仍然无法工作，原因很简单，我留下了几块形状奇怪的金属碎片，它们似乎不适合任何地方。

words.en: I gave up in despair.
words.zh: 我绝望地放弃了。

words.en: The weeks passed and the grass grew.
words.zh: 几个星期过去了，草长起来了。

words.en: When my wife nagged me to do something about it, I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
words.zh: 当我的妻子缠着我做点什么时，我告诉她，要么我必须买一台新割草机，要么让草继续生长。

words.en: Needless to say our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
words.zh: 不用说，我们的房子现在被丛林包围了。

words.en: Buried somewhere in deep grass there is a rusting lawn mower which I have promised to repair one day.
words.zh: 深草丛中的某个地方埋着一台生锈的割草机，我答应有一天会修理它。

words.en: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, overindustrialized planet.
words.zh: 污染是我们为人口过剩、工业化过度的星球付出的代价。

words.en: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
words.zh: 仔细想想，处理垃圾只有四种方法：倾倒、焚烧、将其变成可以再次使用的东西、尝试减少垃圾的产生。

words.en: We keep trying all four methods, but sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.
words.zh: 我们一直在尝试所有四种方法，但我们在世界范围内产生的大量垃圾可能会让我们不知所措。

words.en: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.
words.zh: 然而，垃圾只是污染地球问题的一部分。

words.en: The need to produce ever increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.
words.zh: 生产越来越多的廉价食品的需求导致了另一种污染。

words.en: Industriallized farming metheods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.
words.zh: 工业化农业方法生产廉价的肉类产品：牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。

words.en: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
words.zh: 使用杀虫剂和化肥生产廉价的谷物和蔬菜。

words.en: The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
words.zh: 我们为廉价食品支付的价格可能已经太高了：牛中的疯牛病（BSE）、鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌以及乳制品中的李斯特菌。

words.en: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian, you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables, or just having an innocent glass of water!
words.zh: 如果您认为自己会放弃肉类并成为素食主义者，那么每次您认为自己正在吃新鲜的沙拉和蔬菜，或者只是喝一杯无害的水时，您都可以选择非常昂贵的有机种植的蔬菜或稳定的杀虫剂饮食！

words.en: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban area and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.
words.zh: 然而，还有一种更隐蔽的污染，尤其影响城市地区并侵入我们的日常生活，那就是噪音。

words.en: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
words.zh: 防盗警报在白天或晚上的任何时间响起，只会惹恼路人，实际上会帮助窃贼入室行窃。

words.en: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.
words.zh: 街上的汽车警报器不断地向我们尖叫，令人深感恼火。

words.en: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?) that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.
words.zh: 最近一项关于噪音影响的调查显示（令人惊讶？），夜间不断吠叫的狗将噪音污染列为最高形式，等级范围从 1 到 7。

words.en: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.
words.zh: 调查显示了大量我们非常不喜欢的噪音源。

words.en: Lawn mowers whining on a summer's day, late-night parties in apartment blocks, noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds, especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages, planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
words.zh: 夏日割草机的呜呜声、公寓楼里的深夜聚会、吵闹的邻居、各种车辆，尤其是轰鸣着穿过安静村庄的大型集装箱卡车、头顶上飞过的飞机和直升机、公共场所随身携带并开到最大音量的大型收音机。

words.en: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.
words.zh: 新技术也对噪音做出了自己的贡献。

words.en: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurant or on public transport.
words.zh: 许多人反对使用手机，尤其是在餐厅或公共交通工具等公共场所使用手机时。

words.en: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.
words.zh: 手机上的大声交谈会侵入我们的思绪，或者打断与朋友安静聊天的乐趣。

words.en: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.
words.zh: 噪音污染调查揭示了一种相当令人惊讶且可能有趣的老式噪音源。

words.en: It turned out to be snoring!
words.zh: 原来是打呼噜！

words.en: Men were found to be the worst offenders.
words.zh: 研究发现，男性是最严重的犯罪者。

words.en: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.
words.zh: 据透露，30 岁左右的男性中有 20% 打鼾。

words.en: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
words.zh: 这个数字在 60 多岁的男性中上升到惊人的 60%。

words.en: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly, while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
words.zh: 根据这些数字，我们发现只有 5% 的女性经常打鼾，而其余的女性则经常被她们的伴侣吵醒或保持清醒。

words.en: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.
words.zh: 无论噪音的来源是什么，有一点是肯定的：沉默似乎已成为一段金色的记忆。

words.en: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.
words.zh: 在这个人迹罕至的世界里，仍然有成千上万的地方是游客无法进入的。

words.en: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable.
words.zh: 我们总以为偏远地方的村民是友善好客的。

words.en: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
words.zh: 但那些不仅与外国游客隔绝，甚至与本国同胞隔绝的人也可能对旅行者充满敌意。

words.en: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable — as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
words.zh: 参观真正偏远的村庄很少是令人愉快的——正如我和妻子在巴尔干半岛旅行中发现的那样。

words.en: We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
words.zh: 我们在一个小镇待了几天，参观了附近的一些古老的教堂。

words.en: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
words.zh: 这些吸引了许多游客，因为它们不仅具有巨大的建筑价值，而且还包含大量保存完好的壁画。

words.en: On the day before our departure, several bus loads of tourists descended on the town.
words.zh: 在我们出发的前一天，几辆满载游客的巴士来到了小镇。

words.en: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
words.zh: 这超出了我们的承受能力，所以我们决定在最后一天探索乡村。

words.en: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood.
words.zh: 我们沿着一条出城的小路，穿过几片田野，来到一片茂密的树林前。

words.en: We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
words.zh: 我们原以为这条路会突然结束，但我们发现它是穿过树林的。

words.en: We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream.
words.zh: 我们在树林里走了两个多小时，才来到一条深溪边。

words.en: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
words.zh: 我们可以看到小路在另一边继续延伸，但我们不知道如何穿过小溪。

words.en: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank.
words.zh: 突然，我妻子发现岸边停泊着一艘船。

words.en: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
words.zh: 里面有一个船夫正在熟睡。

words.en: We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
words.zh: 我们轻轻地叫醒了他，请他载我们到对岸。

words.en: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
words.zh: 尽管他一开始不愿意，但我们最终还是说服了他带我们去。

words.en: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
words.zh: 这条路通向一个坐落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。

words.en: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
words.zh: 这个地方有一条杂乱无章的未修筑的道路，两侧排列着小房子。

words.en: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
words.zh: 即使在晴朗的蓝天下，这个村庄也显得令人生畏，因为所有的房屋都是用灰色的泥砖建造的。

words.en: The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
words.zh: 这个村庄似乎荒无人烟，唯一的生命迹象是附近田野里一棵树上拴着一只丑陋的黑山羊。

words.en: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines and had a picnic lunch.
words.zh: 我们坐在田野附近破旧的木栅栏上，打开几罐沙丁鱼，吃了一顿野餐午餐。

words.en: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
words.zh: 突然，我发现妻子似乎充满了惊慌。

words.en: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently as we ate.
words.zh: 抬头一看，我们周围都是衣衫褴褛的孩子，他们一边吃饭，一边默默地看着我们。

words.en: We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless.
words.zh: 我们给他们提供食物并亲切地与他们交谈，但他们仍然一动不动。

words.en: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
words.zh: 我得出的结论是，他们只是害怕陌生人。

words.en: When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
words.zh: 后来，当我们沿着村庄的主要街道行走时，后面跟着一队沉默的孩子们。

words.en: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
words.zh: 原本看似荒凉的村庄，立刻变得生机勃勃。

words.en: Faces appeared at windows.
words.zh: 窗户上出现了面孔。

words.en: Men in shirt sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us.
words.zh: 穿着衬衫的男人站在他们的房子外面，怒视着我们。

words.en: Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways.
words.zh: 披着黑色披肩的老妇人在门口凝视着我们。

words.en: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
words.zh: 最可怕的是，听不到任何声音。

words.en: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
words.zh: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的访客。

words.en: We needed no further warning.
words.zh: 我们不需要进一步的警告。

words.en: Turning back down the main street, we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
words.zh: 沿着主街折返，我们加快了脚步，快步朝小溪走去，希望船夫已经在那里等候了。

words.en: It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.
words.zh: 幸好我的哈丽特阿姨几年前就去世了。

words.en: If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.
words.zh: 如果她今天还活着，她将无法就她最喜欢的话题：家庭佣人发表自己的看法。

words.en: Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.
words.zh: 哈丽特阿姨生活在那个悠闲的时代，雇佣仆人做家务。

words.en: She had a huge, rambling country house called 'The Gables'.
words.zh: 她有一座巨大而杂乱的乡间别墅，名叫“山墙”。

words.en: She was sentimentally attached to this house, for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband's death.
words.zh: 她对这所房子怀有感情，因为尽管它对于她的需要来说太大了，但在她丈夫去世很久之后，她仍然坚持住在那里。

words.en: Before she grew old, aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.
words.zh: 哈丽特姨妈在年老之前，常常挥霍无度地招待客人。

words.en: I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.
words.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我经常参观山墙。

words.en: No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.
words.zh: 无论有多少客人在场，这座大房子总是一尘不染。

words.en: The parquet floors shone like mirrors; highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets; even my uncle's huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.
words.zh: 镶木地板像镜子一样闪闪发光。高度抛光的银器陈列在闪闪发光的玻璃柜中；就连我叔叔的大量藏书也奇迹般地没有沾染灰尘。

words.en: Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned, and polished.
words.zh: 哈丽特姨妈带领着一支无形的仆人大军，不断地擦洗、清洁和擦亮。

words.en: She always referred to them as 'the shifting population', for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.
words.zh: 她总是称他们为“流动人口”，因为他们来来去去的频率如此之高，以至于我什至没有机会知道他们的名字。

words.en: Though my aunt pursued what was, in those days an enlightened policy, in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.
words.zh: 尽管我姨妈奉行的是当时开明的政策，从不允许家政人员每天工作超过八小时，但她却很难取悦。

words.en: While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature, she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days, even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.
words.zh: 虽然她总是批评人性的善变，但她直到生命的最后一刻都坚持不懈地寻找理想的仆人，即使在她对贝西的幻想破灭之后也是如此。

words.en: Bessie worked for aunt Harriet for three years.
words.zh: 贝西为哈丽特姨妈工作了三年。

words.en: During that time she so gained my aunt's confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.
words.zh: 在那段时间里，她赢得了姨妈的信任，并被安排负责家政工作。

words.en: Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie's industriousness and efficiency.
words.zh: 哈丽特姨妈找不到言语来赞扬贝西的勤劳和效率。

words.en: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.
words.zh: 除了所有其他资格外，贝西还是一位专业厨师。

words.en: She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her 'little weakness'.
words.zh: 在哈丽特阿姨发现她的“小弱点”之前，她扮演了三年完美仆人的角色。

words.en: After being absent from The Gables for a week, my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.
words.zh: 离开山墙庄园一周后，有一天下午，姨妈意外地带着一群客人回来了，并指示贝西准备晚餐。

words.en: Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.
words.zh: 不仅饭菜远低于平时的标准，而且贝西走路也似乎无法平稳。

words.en: She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.
words.zh: 她撞到家具上，不停地嘀咕着客人的事。

words.en: When she came in with the last course — a huge pudding — she tripped on the carpet and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.
words.zh: 当她端着最后一道菜——一个巨大的布丁——进来时，她在地毯上绊了一跤，布丁在空中飞了起来，险些撞到了我姨妈，然后用相当大的力量摔在了餐桌上。

words.en: Though this caused great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.
words.zh: 尽管这在客人中引起了极大的欢笑，但哈里特阿姨还是感到震惊。

words.en: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.
words.zh: 她无奈地得出结论：贝西喝醉了。

words.en: The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them and, long before the final catastrophe, had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.
words.zh: 当然，从贝西为他们打开门的那一刻起，客人们就意识到了这一点，而且早在最后的灾难发生之前，他们就很难掩饰他们的乐趣。

words.en: The poor girl was dismissed instantly.
words.zh: 这个可怜的女孩立即被解雇了。

words.en: After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie's wardrobe.
words.zh: 离开后，哈丽特阿姨发现贝西曾经的衣柜里整齐地堆放着成堆的形状各异、大小不一的空酒瓶。

words.en: They had mysteriously found their way there from the wine cellar!
words.zh: 他们竟然从酒窖神秘地找到了路！

words.en: The New Year is a time for resolutions.
words.zh: 新年是制定决心的时候。

words.en: Mentally, at least, most of us could compile formidable lists of 'dos' and 'don'ts'.
words.zh: 至少在精神上，我们大多数人都可以列出令人敬畏的“该做”和“不该做”清单。

words.en: The same old favourites recur year in year out with monotonous regularity.
words.zh: 年复一年，同样的旧爱以单调的规律重复出现。

words.en: We resolve to get up earlier each morning, eat less, find more time to play with the children, do a thousand and one jobs about the house, be nice to people we don't like, drive carefully, and take the dog for a walk every day.
words.zh: 我们决心每天早上早点起床，少吃点东西，多找点时间和孩子们一起玩，做一千零一项关于房子的工作，善待我们不喜欢的人，小心开车，每天遛狗。

words.en: Past experience has taught us that certain accomplishments are beyond attainment.
words.zh: 过去的经验告诉我们，某些成就是无法达到的。

words.en: If we remain inveterate smokers, it is only because we have so often experienced the frustration that results from failure.
words.zh: 如果我们仍然是老烟民，那只是因为我们经常经历失败带来的挫败感。

words.en: Most of us fail in our efforts at sel-improvement because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.
words.zh: 我们大多数人在自我完善的努力中都失败了，因为我们的计划过于雄心勃勃，而我们从来没有时间去实施它们。

words.en: We also make the fundamental error of announcing our resolutions to everybody so that we look even more foolish when we slip back into our bad old ways.
words.zh: 我们还犯了一个根本性的错误，那就是向所有人宣布我们的决议，这样当我们又回到糟糕的旧方式时，我们就会显得更加愚蠢。

words.en: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.
words.zh: 意识到这些陷阱，今年我试图将自己的决心保密。

words.en: I limited myself to two modest ambitions: to do physical exercises every morning and to read more of an evening.
words.zh: 我把自己限制在两个适度的目标上：每天早上锻炼身体，晚上多读书。

words.en: An all-night party on New Year's Eve provided me with a good excuse for not carrying out either of these new resolutions on the first day of the year, but on the second, I applied myself assiduously to the task.
words.zh: 除夕夜的通宵聚会为我在年初一不执行这些新决议提供了很好的借口，但在第二天，我就认真地完成了这项任务。

words.en: The daily exercises lasted only eleven minutes and I proposed to do them early in the morning before anyone had got up.
words.zh: 每天的练习只持续十一分钟，我建议一大早在大家起床之前进行。

words.en: The self-discipline required to drag myself out of bed 11 minutes earlier than usual was considerable.
words.zh: 比平常早 11 分钟起床所需的自律是相当大的。

words.en: Nevertheless, I managed to creep down into the living room for two days before anyone found me out.
words.zh: 尽管如此，我还是设法溜进客厅两天，才被人发现。

words.en: After jumping about on the carpet and twisting the human frame into uncomfortable positions, I sat down at the breakfast table in an exhausted condition.
words.zh: 在地毯上跳来跳去，把人体扭成不舒服的姿势后，我疲惫不堪地坐在早餐桌旁。

words.en: It was this that betrayed me.
words.zh: 正是这个背叛了我。

words.en: The next morning the whole family trooped in to watch the performance.
words.zh: 第二天一早，全家人都成群结队地来看演出。

words.en: That was really unsettling but I fended off the taunts and jibes of the family good-humouredly and soon everybody got used to the idea.
words.zh: 这确实令人不安，但我幽默地抵御了家人的嘲讽和嘲笑，很快每个人都习惯了这个想法。

words.en: However, my enthusiasm waned.
words.zh: 然而，我的热情却减退了。

words.en: The time I spent at exercises gradually diminished.
words.zh: 我花在锻炼上的时间逐渐减少。

words.en: Little by little the eleven minutes fell to zero.
words.zh: 十一点一点一点地减到零。

words.en: By January 10th, I was back to where I had started from.
words.zh: 到1月10日，我又回到了起点。

words.en: I argued that if I spent less time exhausting myself at exercises in the morning, I would keep my mind fresh for reading when I got home from work.
words.zh: 我认为，如果我早上少花点时间锻炼身体，那么下班回家后我就能保持清醒的头脑来阅读。

words.en: Resisting the hypnotizing effect of television, I sat in my room for a few evenings with my eyes glued to a book.
words.zh: 为了抵制电视的催眠作用，我连续几个晚上坐在房间里，眼睛盯着一本书。

words.en: One night, however, feeling cold and lonely, I went downstairs and sat in front of the television pretending to read.
words.zh: 然而有一天晚上，我感到又冷又孤独，就下楼坐在电视机前假装看书。

words.en: That proved to be my undoing, for I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.
words.zh: 事实证明，这就是我的失败，因为我很快又恢复了在屏幕前打瞌睡的坏习惯。

words.en: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.
words.zh: 我仍然没有放弃多读书的决心。

words.en: In fact, I have just bought a book entitled How to Read a Thousand Words a Minute.
words.zh: 事实上，我刚刚买了一本名为《如何每分钟阅读千字》的书。

words.en: Perhaps it will solve my problem, but I just haven't had time to read it!
words.zh: 也许它可以解决我的问题，但我只是没有时间阅读它！

words.en: Predicting the future is notoriously difficult.
words.zh: 预测未来是出了名的困难。

words.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example, that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
words.zh: 例如，在 20 世纪 70 年代中期，谁能想象到到 20 世纪末，电脑会像电视机一样普遍出现在人们的家庭中？

words.en: In the 1970s, computers were common enough, but only in big business, government departments and large organizations.
words.zh: 在 20 世纪 70 年代，计算机已经很常见，但仅限于大企业、政府部门和大型组织。

words.en: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
words.zh: 这些就是所谓的大型机。

words.en: Mainframe computers were very large indeed often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms, employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
words.zh: 大型计算机确实非常大，经常占据整个空调房间，雇用全职技术人员并运行专门编写的软件。

words.en: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
words.zh: 尽管这些大型机器仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已被小型强大的个人计算机（通常称为 PC）所取代。

words.en: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.
words.zh: 1975 年，一款名为 Altair 的原始机器在美国推出。

words.en: It can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and it pointed the way to the future.
words.zh: 它可以恰当地描述为第一台“家用计算机”，它为未来指明了道路。

words.en: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.
words.zh: 随后，在 20 世纪 70 年代末，一款名为 Apple 的机器问世。

words.en: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world's first Personal Computer.
words.zh: 20世纪80年代初，计算机巨头IBM生产了世界上第一台个人计算机。

words.en: This ran on an 'operating system' called DOS, produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
words.zh: 它运行在一个名为 DOS 的“操作系统”上，该操作系统由当时一家名为微软的小公司生产。

words.en: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
words.zh: IBM 个人计算机被广泛复制。

words.en: From those humble beginnings, we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
words.zh: 从那些不起眼的开始，我们见证了当今普遍使用的用户友好型家用计算机和多媒体机的发展。

words.en: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman, Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
words.zh: 考虑到这些发展是最近才发生的，更值得注意的是，早在 20 世纪 60 年代，英国人 Leon Bagrit 就能够预测我们今天所知道的计算机的一些用途。

words.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and would 'rule the world', which people liked to believe in those days.
words.zh: 巴格里特驳斥了当时人们喜欢相信的计算机将学会为自己“思考”并“统治世界”的想法。

words.en: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alterative routes, when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses, when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
words.zh: 巴格里特预见到有一天，计算机将小到可以握在手中，届时它们将能够提供有关交通拥堵的信息并建议替代路线，届时它们将在医院中用于帮助医生诊断疾病，届时它们将使办公室工作人员和会计师摆脱枯燥、重复的文书工作。

words.en: All these computer uses have become commonplace.
words.zh: 所有这些计算机的使用已经变得司空见惯。

words.en: Of course, Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet, the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
words.zh: 当然，莱昂·巴格里特不可能预见到互联网的发展，互联网是一个全球性的系统，使我们能够通过使用连接到电话网络的计算机与世界任何地方的任何人进行即时通信。

words.en: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject, so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
words.zh: 他也无法预见我们如何使用互联网来获取每个已知主题的信息，这样我们就可以在家里的屏幕上阅读它，如果我们愿意的话，甚至还可以打印它。

words.en: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.
words.zh: 计算机变得越来越小，功能越来越强大，而且越来越便宜。

words.en: This is what makes Leon Bagrit's predictions particularly remarkable.
words.zh: 这就是莱昂·巴格里特的预测尤为引人注目的原因。

words.en: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
words.zh: 如果他或像他这样的人今天还活着，他也许能够告诉我们未来五十年会发生什么。

words.en: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
words.zh: 我的表弟哈利在他的书房里永久展示着一个形状奇特的大瓶子。

words.en: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green, an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
words.zh: 尽管瓶子呈微妙的绿色，但细心的参观者很快就会注意到它装满了看起来像厚厚的灰色物质。

words.en: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
words.zh: 如果你问哈利瓶子里装的是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是有香味的泥土。

words.en: If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.
words.zh: 如果你表示怀疑或惊讶，他会立即邀请你闻一闻，然后将一些擦到你的皮肤上。

words.en: The brief experiment would dispel any further doubts she might have.
words.zh: 这个简短的实验将消除她可能存在的任何进一步的疑虑。

words.en: The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.
words.zh: 瓶子里确实装着香泥。

words.en: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.
words.zh: 哈利如何获得这些稀奇古怪的东西，这是一个他喜欢讲述的有趣故事。

words.en: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
words.zh: 而且，有了这瓶酒，他改掉了多年来养成的坏习惯。

words.en: Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.
words.zh: 哈利曾经认为，走进昂贵的化妆品店并对根本不存在的商品提出无理要求是一个天大的笑话。

words.en: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
words.zh: 他会当场发明一些奇特的名字。

words.en: On entering a shop, he would ask for a new perfume called 'Scented Shadow' or for 'insoluble bath cubes'.
words.zh: 进入商店时，他会索要一种名为“香​​影”的新香水或“不溶性沐浴块”。

words.en: If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
words.zh: 如果店员告诉他她没有听说过，他就会假装很不高兴。

words.en: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
words.zh: 他喜欢被告知他的一款想象中的产品暂时缺货，他会忠实地承诺在将来的某个日期再次打电话，但他当然从未这样做过。

words.en: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
words.zh: 我完全无法理解哈利在这些表演中如何保持板着脸。

words.en: Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.
words.zh: 哈利不需要被提示解释他是如何购买他那瓶珍贵的泥浆的。

words.en: One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for 'Myrolite'.
words.zh: 有一天，他去了伦敦的一家专卖店，要了“Myrolite”。

words.en: The shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable.
words.zh: 店员看上去很困惑，哈利重复了这个词，慢慢地强调每个音节。

words.en: When the woman shook her head in bewilderment, Harry went on to explain that 'myrolite' was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles.
words.zh: 当那位女士困惑地摇摇头时，哈利继续解释说，“香脂石”是一种坚硬的、类似琥珀的物质，可以用来去除雀斑。

words.en: This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.
words.zh: 这个解释显然向那位翻遍货架的女士传达了某种信息。

words.en: She produced all sorts of weird concoctions, but none of them met with Harry's requirements.
words.zh: 她制作了各种奇怪的混合物，但没有一个符合哈利的要求。

words.en: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
words.zh: 当哈利表现出有点生气的样子时，助理答应给他点一些。

words.en: Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.
words.zh: 哈利因自己的成功而陶醉，然后要了加香的泥浆。

words.en: He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment.
words.zh: 他预计助理会惊讶地看着他。

words.en: However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman's eyes immediately lit up and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
words.zh: 然而，轮到他惊讶了，女人立刻眼睛一亮，拿了几个瓶子放在柜台上让哈利检查。

words.en: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
words.zh: 这一次，哈利不得不承认失败。

words.en: He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.
words.zh: 他拿起看似最小的一瓶，小心翼翼地询问了价格。

words.en: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
words.zh: 他很高兴只赚了二十英镑，然后匆忙撤退，腋下夹着珍贵的瓶子。

words.en: From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.
words.zh: 从那时起，哈利决定他发明的这个小游戏可能会很昂贵。

words.en: The curious bottle which now adorns the bookcase in his study was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics.
words.zh: 现在装饰在他书房书柜上的那个奇怪的瓶子是他第一次也是最后一次购买稀有化妆品。

words.en: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies.
words.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚国家因其开明的社会政策而受到全世界的钦佩。

words.en: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers.
words.zh: 瑞典已经形成了一套优秀的制度来保护公民个人免受专横或无能的公职人员的侵害。

words.en: The system has worked so well, that it has been adopted in other countries too.
words.zh: 该系统运行良好，因此也被其他国家采用。

words.en: The Swedes were the first to recognize that public officials like civil servants, police officers, health inspectors or tax-collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public.
words.zh: 瑞典人是第一个认识到公务员、警察、卫生检查员或税务员等公职人员可能会犯错误或过于热心地认为自己是在为公众服务的人。

words.en: As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a scheme to safeguard the interest of the individual.
words.zh: 早在1809年，瑞典议会就推出了一项保护个人利益的计划。

words.en: A parliamentary committee representing all political parties appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the State.
words.zh: 代表所有政党的议会委员会任命一名有适当资格的人员来调查私人对国家的不满。

words.en: The official title of the person is 'Justiteombudsman', but the Swedes commonly refer to him as the 'J.O.' or 'Ombudsman'.
words.zh: 此人的官方头衔是“Justiteombudsman”，但瑞典人通常称他为“J.O.”或“监察员”。

words.en: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
words.zh: 监察员不受政治压力。

words.en: He investigates complaints large and small that come to him from all levels of society.
words.zh: 他调查社会各阶层向他提出的大大小小的投诉。

words.en: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1,200 letters a year.
words.zh: 由于投诉必须以书面形式提出，监察员平均每年收到 1,200 封信函。

words.en: He has eight lawyer assistants to help him and he examines every single letter in detail.
words.zh: 他有八名律师助理来帮助他，他会详细检查每一封信。

words.en: There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman's work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection.
words.zh: 监察员的工作没有什么秘密，因为他的信件可供公众查阅。

words.en: If a citizen's complaint is justified the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
words.zh: 如果公民的投诉合理，监察员将代表他采取行动。

words.en: The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint.
words.zh: 他采取的行动根据投诉的性质而有所不同。

words.en: He may gently reprimand an official or even suggest to parliament that a law be altered.
words.zh: 他可能会温和地谴责官员，甚至建议议会修改法律。

words.en: The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work.
words.zh: 以下案例是监察员工作的典型例子。

words.en: A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police, simply because he was a foreigner.
words.zh: 一名居住在瑞典村庄的外国人写信给监察员，抱怨他仅仅因为是外国人而受到警察的虐待。

words.en: The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the Chief of Police in the district asking him to send a record of the case.
words.zh: 监察员立即写信给该地区的警察局长，要求他发送案件记录。

words.en: There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified and the Chief of Police strongly denied the accusation.
words.zh: 记录中没有任何内容表明外国人的投诉是合理的，警察局长强烈否认了这一指控。

words.en: It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action, but when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village, he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter.
words.zh: 监察员不可能采取行动，但当他收到同村另一名外国人的类似投诉时，他立即派了一名律师调查此事。

words.en: The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions.
words.zh: 律师查明，一名警察确实多次粗暴地对待外国人。
