words.en: The fact that the policeman was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files.
words.zh: 这名警察对外国人存在偏见的事实无法记录在官方档案中。

words.en: It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts.
words.zh: 监察员只能派一名代表去核实事实，才能弄清楚这一点。

words.en: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
words.zh: 该名警察受到严厉谴责，并被告知，如果再对他提出投诉，他将被起诉。

words.en: The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
words.zh: 监察员的迅速行动立即结束了可能被忽视的令人不快的做法。

words.en: We have been brought up to fear insects.
words.zh: 我们从小就害怕昆虫。

words.en: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
words.zh: 我们认为它们是不必要的生物，弊大于利。

words.en: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
words.zh: 我们不断地向它们发动战争，因为它们污染我们的食物、传播疾病或吞噬我们的庄稼。

words.en: They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
words.zh: 它们会在没有任何挑衅的情况下蜇人或咬人；夏天的夜晚，它们会不请自来地飞进我们的房间，或者敲打我们亮着灯的窗户。

words.en: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
words.zh: 我们不仅害怕蜘蛛或黄蜂等令人讨厌的昆虫，还害怕飞蛾等无害的昆虫。

words.en: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.
words.zh: 阅读它们会增加我们的理解，但不会消除我们的恐惧。

words.en: Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organized society does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
words.zh: 知道勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一个高度组织化的社会中，当我们发现成群结队的蚂蚁在精心准备的野餐午餐上爬行时，我们仍然会感到充满厌恶。

words.en: No matter how much we like honey, or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
words.zh: 无论我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，或者我们读过多少关于蜜蜂所拥有的不可思议的方向感的文章，我们都害怕被蜇伤。

words.en: Most of our fears are unreasonable, but they are impossible to erase.
words.zh: 我们大多数的恐惧都是不合理的，但却无法消除。

words.en: At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
words.zh: 然而，与此同时，昆虫却有着奇异的魅力。

words.en: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
words.zh: 我们喜欢阅读有关它们的文章，尤其是当我们发现它们像螳螂一样过着极其可怕的生活时。

words.en: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware (we hope) of our presence.
words.zh: 我们喜欢盯着他们，着迷地看着他们忙着自己的事情，而没有意识到（我们希望）我们的存在。

words.en: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly, or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle?
words.zh: 谁没有看到一只蜘蛛扑向一只苍蝇，或者一队蚂蚁胜利地将一只巨大的死甲虫带回家时感到敬畏？

words.en: Last summer I spent days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
words.zh: 去年夏天，我在花园里呆了几天，看着成千上万的蚂蚁爬上我心爱的桃树的树干。

words.en: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
words.zh: 这棵树靠在房子有遮蔽的一面温暖的墙上生长。

words.en: I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
words.zh: 我特别为它感到骄傲，不仅因为它熬过了几个严冬，还因为它偶尔结出甘美的桃子。

words.en: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
words.zh: 夏天的时候，我发现树上的叶子开始枯萎。

words.en: Clusters of tiny insects called aphides were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
words.zh: 在叶子的背面发现了一群被称为蚜虫的小昆虫。

words.en: They were visited by a large colony of ants which obtained a sort of honey from them.
words.zh: 一大群蚂蚁拜访了他们，并从他们身上获取了一种蜂蜜。

words.en: I immediately embarked on an experiment which even though it failed to get rid of the ants kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
words.zh: 我立即开始了一项实验，尽管没能消灭蚂蚁，但它却让我着迷了二十四小时。

words.en: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphides.
words.zh: 我用胶带把树的根部绑起来，使蚂蚁无法接触到蚜虫。

words.en: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
words.zh: 胶带太粘了，他们不敢越过它。

words.en: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
words.zh: 很长一段时间，我都困惑地看着它们在树下跑来跑去。

words.en: I even went out at midnight with a torch and noted with satisfaction (and surprise) that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
words.zh: 我什至半夜拿着手电筒出去，满意地（也惊讶地）注意到蚂蚁仍然在胶带周围聚集，却无能为力。

words.en: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
words.zh: 第二天一早我就起床了，希望看到蚂蚁们已经绝望地放弃了。

words.en: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
words.zh: 相反，我看到他们发现了一条新路线。

words.en: They were climbing up the wall of the house and then on to the leaves of the tree.
words.zh: 他们爬上房子的墙壁，然后爬上树叶。

words.en: I realized sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.
words.zh: 我悲伤地意识到我已经彻底被他们的聪明才智打败了。

words.en: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods!
words.zh: 蚂蚁们很快就找到了我完全不科学的方法的答案！

words.en: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
words.zh: 天文学的最新发展使得探测银河系和其他星系中的行星成为可能。

words.en: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
words.zh: 这是一项重大成就，因为相对而言，行星非常小并且不发光。

words.en: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
words.zh: 事实证明，寻找行星已经够困难的了，但在行星上寻找生命则更加困难。

words.en: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
words.zh: 首先要回答的问题是行星是否真的能够维持生命。

words.en: In our own solar system, for example, Venus is far to hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
words.zh: 例如，在我们的太阳系中，金星太热，而火星太冷，无法维持生命。

words.en: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
words.zh: 只有地球提供了理想的条件，即使在这里，植物和动物的生命进化也需要超过四十亿年。

words.en: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its 'sun'.
words.zh: 一颗行星能否维持生命取决于其恒星（即“太阳”）的大小和亮度。

words.en: Imagine a star up to twenty times larger, brighter and hotter than our own sun.
words.zh: 想象一颗比我们的太阳大二十倍、更亮、更热的恒星。

words.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
words.zh: 一颗行星必须距离它很远才能维持生命。

words.en: Alternatively, if the star were small, the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
words.zh: 或者，如果恒星很小，那么支持生命的行星就必须有一个靠近它的轨道，并为生命形式的发展提供完美的条件。

words.en: But how would we find such a planet?
words.zh: 但我们怎样才能找到这样一颗行星呢？

words.en: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
words.zh: 目前，还没有任何望远镜能够探测到生命的存在。

words.en: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the 21st century.
words.zh: 这种望远镜的研制将是21世纪最伟大的天文工程之一。

words.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
words.zh: 使用地球望远镜不可能在另一个星球上寻找生命。

words.en: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
words.zh: 我们自己温暖的大气层和望远镜产生的热量将使得我们无法探测到像行星这样小的物体。

words.en: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope, would not be suitable because of the dust particles in our solar system.
words.zh: 即使是绕地球轨道运行的望远镜，例如非常成功的哈勃望远镜，也因为太阳系中的尘埃颗粒而不再适用。

words.en: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
words.zh: 望远镜必须距离木星那么远才能在外太空寻找生命，因为我们越靠近太阳系的外缘，尘埃就会变得越薄。

words.en: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star, so that we would be able to 'see' the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
words.zh: 一旦我们发现了一颗行星，我们就必须找到一种方法来遮挡来自其恒星的光线，这样我们就能够正确地“看到”这颗行星并分析它的大气层。

words.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.
words.zh: 首先，我们会寻找植物生命，而不是“小绿人”。

words.en: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.
words.zh: 最有可能在行星上发展的生命形式是细菌。

words.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
words.zh: 正是细菌产生了我们在地球上呼吸的氧气。

words.en: For most of the earth's history they have been the only form of life on our planet.
words.zh: 在地球历史的大部分时间里，它们一直是我们星球上唯一的生命形式。

words.en: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
words.zh: 作为地球人，我们总是希望小绿人能够来拜访我们，并能够与他们交流。

words.en: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
words.zh: 但这种希望始终只存在于科幻小说的领域。

words.en: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
words.zh: 如果我们能够在另一个星球上发现像细菌这样的低等生命形式，那将彻底改变我们对自己的看法。

words.en: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.
words.zh: 正如美国宇航局的丹尼尔·戈尔丁（Daniel Goldin）所说，“在其他地方寻找生命将会改变一切。”

words.en: No human endeavour or thought would be unchanged by it.'
words.zh: 人类的努力或思想不会因此而改变。

words.en: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.
words.zh: 构成我们农场东部边界的河流一直在我们的生活中发挥着重要作用。

words.en: Without it we could not make a living.
words.zh: 没有它我们就无法谋生。

words.en: There is only enough spring water to supply the needs of the house so we have to pump from the river for farm use.
words.zh: 泉水只能满足房屋的需要，所以我们必须从河里抽水用于农田使用。

words.en: We tell the river all our secrets.
words.zh: 我们告诉河流我们所有的秘密。

words.en: We know instinctively, just as beekeepers with their bees, that misfortune might overtake us if the important events of our lives were not related to it.
words.zh: 我们本能地知道，就像养蜂人和他们的蜜蜂一样，如果我们生活中的重要事件与不幸无关，不幸可能会降临到我们身上。

words.en: We have special river birthday parties in the summer.
words.zh: 夏天我们会举办特别的河流生日派对。

words.en: Sometimes we go upstream to a favourite backwater, sometimes we have our party at the boathouse, which a predecessor of ours at the farm built in the meadow hard by the deepest pool for swimming and diving.
words.zh: 有时我们会逆流而上，到达最喜欢的回水地，有时我们会在船库举行聚会，船库是我们农场的前身在最深的水池旁边的草地上建造的，用于游泳和潜水。

words.en: In a heat wave we choose a midnight birthday party and that is the most exciting of all.
words.zh: 在热浪中，我们选择了午夜生日聚会，这是最令人兴奋的。

words.en: We welcome the seasons by the riverside, crowning the youngest girl with flowers in the spring, holding a summer festival on Midsummer Eve, giving thanks for the harvest in the autumn, and throwing a holly wreath into the current in the winter.
words.zh: 我们在河边迎接季节，春天给小姑娘戴花，仲夏夜举行夏祭，秋天感谢丰收，冬天把冬青花环扔进河里。

words.en: After a long period of rain the river may overflow its banks.
words.zh: 经过长时间的降雨后，河水可能会溢出河岸。

words.en: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.
words.zh: 这种情况很少见，因为我们的气候很少走向极端。

words.en: We are lucky in that only the lower fields, which make up a very small proportion of our farm, are affected by flooding, but other farms are less favourably sited, and flooding can sometimes spell disaster for their owners.
words.zh: 我们很幸运，只有地势较低的田地（占我们农场的一小部分）受到洪水的影响，但其他农场的位置较差，洪水有时会给农场主带来灾难。

words.en: One bad winter we watched the river creep up the lower meadows.
words.zh: 在一个严酷的冬天，我们看到河水顺着低处的草地缓缓流淌。

words.en: All the cattle had been moved into stalls and we stood to lose little.
words.zh: 所有的牛都被转移到畜栏里，我们几乎不会损失什么。

words.en: We were, however, worried about our nearest neighbours, whose farm was low lying and who were newcomers to the district.
words.zh: 然而，我们担心最近的邻居，他们的农场地势低洼，而且是该地区的新来者。

words.en: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
words.zh: 由于洪水导致电话无法使用，我们无法得知他们的情况如何。

words.en: From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours, and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
words.zh: 从阁楼的窗户我们可以看到他们的土地与我们的土地相连的那条河的全景，在最关键的时刻我们轮流看守这一点。

words.en: The first sign of disaster was a dead sheep floating down.
words.zh: 灾难的第一个征兆是一只死羊飘落下来。

words.en: Next came a horse, swimming bravely, but we were afraid that the strength of the current would prevent its landing anywhere before it became exhausted.
words.zh: 接下来是一匹马，勇敢地游着，但我们担心水流的力量会阻止它在精疲力竭之前到达任何地方。

words.en: Suddenly a raft appeared, looking rather like Noah's ark, carrying the whole family, a few hens, the dogs, a cat, and a bird in a cage.
words.zh: 突然出现了一个木筏，看起来很像诺亚方舟，载着全家人，还有几只母鸡、狗、一只猫和一只关在笼子里的鸟。

words.en: We realized that they must have become unduly frightened by the rising flood, for their house, which had sound foundations, would have stood stoutly even if it had been almost submerged.
words.zh: 我们意识到，他们一定是被不断上涨的洪水吓坏了，因为他们的房子地基牢固，即使几乎被淹没，也能屹立不倒。

words.en: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boat hooks, in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towrds our bank.
words.zh: 我们家的男人们拿着船钩趟过被水淹没的草地，希望能够抓住木筏的一角，把它从河岸上的水流中拉出来。

words.en: We still think it a miracle that they were able to do so.
words.zh: 我们仍然认为他们能够做到这一点是一个奇迹。

courses.title: Lesson 57 · Back in the Old Country

words.en: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.
words.zh: 我停下来让车冷却一下并研究地图。

words.en: I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me.
words.zh: 我原以为现在已经接近我的目标了，但一切对我来说仍然显得陌生。

words.en: I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago.
words.zh: 当我父亲带我出国时，我才五岁，那是十八年前的事了。

words.en: When my mother had died after a tragic accident, he did not quickly recover from the shock and loneliness.
words.zh: 当我的母亲在一场悲惨的事故后去世时，他并没有很快从震惊和孤独中恢复过来。

words.en: Everything around him was full of her presence, continually reopening the wound.
words.zh: 他周围的一切都充满了她的存在，不断地撕开伤口。

words.en: So he decided to emigrate.
words.zh: 于是他决定移民。

words.en: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.
words.zh: 在新的国家，他全神贯注地为我们两个人创造新的生活，因此他逐渐不再悲伤。

words.en: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman's care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.
words.zh: 他没有再娶，我是在没有女人照顾的情况下长大的；但我什么都不缺，因为他既是我的父亲又是我的母亲。

words.en: He always meant to go back one day, but not to stay.
words.zh: 他总想有一天回去，但又不想留下来。

words.en: His roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new land.
words.zh: 他和我的根已经深深扎根在这片新土地上。

words.en: But he wanted to see the old folk againand to visit my mother's grave.
words.zh: 但他想再次见到老人并参观我母亲的坟墓。

words.en: He became mortally ill a few months before we had planned to go and, when he knew that he was dying, he made me promise to go on my own.
words.zh: 在我们计划出发前几个月，他病重了，当他知道自己快要死时，他让我答应自己去。

words.en: I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps, which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I did not think I should need on the last stage.
words.zh: 着陆后的第二天，我租了一辆车，买了一本综合地图书，我发现这对越野旅行最有帮助，但我认为在最后一个阶段我不需要它。

words.en: It was not that I actually remembered anything at all.
words.zh: 并不是说我真的记得任何事情。

words.en: But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone after leaving the nearest town, so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
words.zh: 但我父亲一遍又一遍地描述了离开最近的城镇后我们在每个里程碑上应该看到的东西，因此我确信我应该将其视为熟悉的领域。

words.en: Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost.
words.zh: 好吧，我错了，因为我现在迷路了。

words.en: I looked at the map and then at the milometer.
words.zh: 我看了看地图，然后又看了看里程表。

words.en: I had come ten miles since leaving the town and at this point, according to my father, I should be looking at farms and cottages in a valley, with the spire of the church of our village showing in the far distance.
words.zh: 我离开小镇已经走了十英里，按照父亲的说法，此时我应该看到山谷里的农场和小屋，远处还可以看到我们村庄教堂的尖顶。

words.en: I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no church spire-only a lake.
words.zh: 我看不到山谷，看不到农场，看不到小屋，也看不到教堂的尖顶——只有一个湖。

words.en: I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere.
words.zh: 我断定我一定是在某个地方转错了方向。

words.en: So I drove back to the town and began to retrace the route, taking frequent glances at the map.
words.zh: 于是我开车回到镇上，开始沿着路线走回去，时不时地看一下地图。

words.en: I landed up at the same corner.
words.zh: 我降落在同一个角落。

words.en: The curious thing was that the lake was not marked on the map.
words.zh: 奇怪的是，地图上没有标出这个湖。

words.en: I felt as if I had stumbled into a nightmare country, as you sometimes do in dreams.
words.zh: 我感觉自己仿佛跌入了一个噩梦般的国家，就像你有时在梦中所做的那样。

words.en: And, as in a nightmare, there was nobody in sight to help me.
words.zh: 而且，就像在噩梦中一样，看不到任何人来帮助我。

words.en: Fortunately for me, as I was wondering what to do next, there appeared on the horizon a man on horseback, riding in my direction.
words.zh: 对我来说幸运的是，当我想知道下一步该做什么时，地平线上出现了一个骑马的人，朝我的方向骑马。

words.en: I waited till he came near, then I asked him the way to our old village.
words.zh: 我等到他走近了，才问他去我们老村子的路。

words.en: He said that there was now no village.
words.zh: 他说现在已经没有村庄了。

words.en: I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name.
words.zh: 我以为他一定误会了我，所以我重复了它的名字。

words.en: This time he pointed to the lake.
words.zh: 这次他指着湖。

words.en: The village no longer existed because it had been submerged, and all the valley too.
words.zh: 村庄已经不复存在，因为它已经被淹没了，整个山谷也被淹没了。

words.en: The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir.
words.zh: 这个湖不是天然的，而是一个人造水库。

words.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.
words.zh: 老太太很高兴回到她住的公寓楼。

words.en: Her shopping had tired her and her basket had grown heavier with every step of the way home.
words.zh: 购物让她疲惫不堪，回家的每一步她的篮子都变得越来越重。

words.en: In the lift her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest; but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
words.zh: 在电梯里，她只想着吃午饭和好好休息。但当她走出自己的楼层时，她突然发现前门开着，把两人都忘记了。

words.en: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence, when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks.
words.zh: 她正在想，第二天早上她必须斥责她的家庭保姆，因为她犯了如此严重的疏忽，这时她想起家庭保姆离开后她去购物了，而且她知道她已经把两把钥匙都插进了锁里。

words.en: She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open, yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
words.zh: 她慢慢地走进大厅，立刻发现所有房间的门都开着，但按照惯例，她出去之前都关上了门。

words.en: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.
words.zh: 她往客厅里一看，写字台边一片混乱。

words.en: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
words.zh: 当时，窃贼显然是在她不在期间强行闯入的。

words.en: Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves, but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her, so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
words.zh: 她的第一反应是去所有的房间寻找小偷，但后来她决定，在她这个年纪，有人陪着她可能会更谨慎，所以她去地下室找了门房。

words.en: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.
words.zh: 这时她的腿开始发抖，于是她坐下来喝了一杯很浓的茶，而他则打电话给警察。

words.en: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter's assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
words.zh: 然后，她恢复了镇静，准备在门房的帮助下出发去寻找可能仍然潜伏在她公寓里的入侵者。

words.en: They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing, as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints.
words.zh: 他们穿过房间，小心翼翼地不碰任何东西，因为他们不想妨碍警察寻找指纹。

words.en: The chaos was inconceivable.
words.zh: 混乱程度难以想象。

words.en: She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding: and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
words.zh: 她在这套公寓里住了三十年，是名副其实的囤积狂人：她拥有的一切似乎都被扔掉了，翻来覆去。

words.en: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
words.zh: 至少现在对她来说整理那些她几年前就应该丢弃的东西变得更容易了。

words.en: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.
words.zh: 然后一名警官带着一名警员到达，她告诉他们她发现了这间被洗劫一空的公寓。

words.en: The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
words.zh: 检查员开始寻找指纹，而警员则检查前门锁是否未被强行打开，从而证明窃贼要么使用万能钥匙，要么从阳台进入。

words.en: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
words.zh: 没有指纹痕迹，但检查员发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包裹，里面装着珠宝，老太太说这些珠宝不是她的。

words.en: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
words.zh: 因此，他们进入这间公寓显然不是窃贼当天的第一份工作，他们肯定受到了打扰。

words.en: The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day, and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
words.zh: 检查员随后要求老太太在第二天之前尝试检查一下缺少的东西，并建议她不要独自在公寓里住几个晚上。

words.en: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
words.zh: 老太太认为他是个挑剔的人，但既然搬运工同意了他的意见，她就给女儿打电话，请求她帮忙解决她所说的一点小麻烦。

words.en: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.
words.zh: 人们倾向于积累财产，有时却没有意识到这样做。

words.en: Indeed they can have a delightful surprise when they find something useful which they did not know they owned.
words.zh: 事实上，当他们发现一些他们不知道自己拥有的有用的东西时，他们会感到惊喜。

words.en: Those who never have to move house become indiscriminate collectors of what can only be described as clutter.
words.zh: 那些从来不用搬家的人就成了乱七八糟的垃圾收集者。

words.en: They leave unwanted objects in drawers, cupboards and attics for years, in the belief that they may one day need just those very things.
words.zh: 他们把不需要的东西留在抽屉、橱柜和阁楼里多年，相信有一天他们可能只需要这些东西。

words.en: As they grow old, people also accumulate belongings for two other reasons, lack of physical and mental energy, both of which are essential in turning out and throwing away, and sentiment.
words.zh: 随着年龄的增长，人们还会因为另外两个原因而积累物品，一是缺乏体力和精神能量（这两者对于扔掉和扔掉都是至关重要的），二是情感。

words.en: Things owned for a long time are full of associations with the past, perhaps with relatives who are dead, and so they gradually acquire a value beyond their true worth.
words.zh: 长期拥有的东西充满了与过去的联系，也许是与已故亲人的联系，因此它们逐渐获得了超越其真实价值的价值。

words.en: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
words.zh: 家里有些东西是故意收集的，以避免浪费。

words.en: Among these I would list string and brown paper, kept by thrifty people when a parcel has been opened, to save buying these two requisites.
words.zh: 其中我会列出绳子和牛皮纸，节俭的人在打开包裹时会保留它们，以节省购买这两种必需品的费用。

words.en: Collecting small items can easily become a mania.
words.zh: 收集小物品很容易成为一种狂热。

words.en: I know someone who always cuts sketches out from newspapers of model clothes that she would like to buy if she had the money.
words.zh: 我认识一个人，她总是从报纸上剪下模特服装的草图，如果她有钱的话，她想买这些衣服。

words.en: As she is not rich, the chances that she will ever be able to afford such purchases are remote; but she is never sufficiently strongminded to be able to stop the practice.
words.zh: 由于她并不富有，因此她买得起此类物品的可能性很小。但她的意志力始终不够坚强，无法阻止这种做法。

words.en: It is a harmless habit, but it litters up her desk to such an extent that every time she opens it, loose bits of paper fall out in every direction.
words.zh: 这是一个无害的习惯，但它在她的桌子上乱七八糟，以至于每次她打开桌子时，松散的纸张碎片都会从各个方向掉下来。

words.en: Collecting as a serious hobby is quite different and has many advantages.
words.zh: 收藏作为一种严肃的爱好是完全不同的，并且有很多优点。

words.en: It provides relaxation for leisure hours, as just looking at one's treasures is always a joy.
words.zh: 它为休闲时光提供了放松，因为仅仅看着自己的宝藏总是一种乐趣。

words.en: One does not have to go outside for amusement, since the collection is housed at home.
words.zh: 人们不必外出娱乐，因为藏品就存放在家里。

words.en: Whatever it consists of, stamps, records, first editions of books, china, glass, antique furniture, pictures, model cars, stuffed birds, toy animals, there is always something to do in connection with it, from finding the right place for the latest addition, to verifying facts in reference books.
words.zh: 无论它由什么组成，邮票、唱片、第一版书籍、瓷器、玻璃、古董家具、图片、模型汽车、毛绒玩具、玩具动物，总有一些与之相关的事情要做，从为最新添加的物品寻找合适的位置，到验证参考书中的事实。

words.en: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.
words.zh: 这种爱好不仅可以教育一个人所选择的学科，还可以教育一个与之相关的一般事物。

words.en: There are also other benefits.
words.zh: 还有其他好处。

words.en: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.
words.zh: 人们想要结识志趣相投的收藏家，寻求建议，交换意见，交换文章，展示最新的发现。

words.en: So one's circle of friends grows.
words.zh: 这样一个人的朋友圈就扩大了。

words.en: Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town, possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
words.zh: 很快，这种爱好就会导致旅行，也许是在另一个城镇举行会议，也可能是出国旅行寻找稀有标本，因为收藏家并不局限于任何一个国家。

words.en: Over the years, one may well become an authority on one's hobby and will very probably be asked to give informal talks to little gatherings and then, if successful, to larger audiences.
words.zh: 多年来，一个人很可能会成为自己爱好的权威，并且很可能会被要求在小型聚会上进行非正式演讲，如果成功的话，还会向更多的观众进行演讲。

words.en: In this way self-confidence grows, first from mastering a subject, then from being able to talk about it.
words.zh: 通过这种方式，自信首先来自于掌握一门学科，然后来自于能够谈论它。

words.en: Collecting, by occupying spare time so constructively, makes a person contented, with no time for boredom.
words.zh: 收集，通过如此建设性地占用业余时间，使人感到满足，没有时间感到无聊。

courses.title: Lesson 60 · Too Early and Too Late

words.en: Punctuality is a necessary habit in all public affairs in civilized society.
words.zh: 守时是文明社会一切公共事务的必备习惯。

words.en: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.
words.zh: 没有它，任何事情都无法得出结论。一切都将处于混乱状态。

words.en: Only in a sparsely-populated rural community is it possible to disregard it.
words.zh: 只有在人烟稀少的农村社区才有可能忽视它。

words.en: In ordinary living, there can be some tolerance of unpunctuality.
words.zh: 在日常生活中，不守时是可以容忍的。

words.en: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.
words.zh: 知识分子正在研究一些深奥的问题，他们手头上的事情已经协调和组织好了。

words.en: He is therefore forgiven if late for a dinner party.
words.zh: 因此，如果他参加晚宴迟到，也是可以原谅的。

words.en: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
words.zh: 但当人们唯一的过错就是把事情做得很好时，他们常常会因为不守时而受到指责。

words.en: It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time, so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
words.zh: 对于精力充沛、思维敏捷的人来说，很难浪费时间，因此他们常常想在出发去赴约之前先完成工作。

words.en: If no accidents occur on the way, like punctured tyres, diversions of traffic, sudden descent of fog, they will be on time.
words.zh: 如果途中没有发生任何意外，比如轮胎扎破、交通改道、突然起雾，他们就会准时到达。

words.en: They are often more industrious, useful citizens than those who are never late.
words.zh: 他们往往比那些从不迟到的人更勤奋、更有用。

words.en: The over-punctual can be as much a trial to others as the unpunctual.
words.zh: 过于准时和不准时一样，对他人来说也是一种考验。

words.en: The guest who arrives half an hour too soon is the greatest nuisance.
words.zh: 迟到半小时的客人是最大的麻烦。

words.en: Some friends of my family had this irritating habit.
words.zh: 我家人的一些朋友有这种令人恼火的习惯。

words.en: The only thing to do was ask them to come half an hour later than the other guests.
words.zh: 唯一能做的就是让他们比其他客人晚来半个小时。

words.en: Then they arrived just when we wanted them.
words.zh: 然后他们就在我们需要的时候到达了。

words.en: If you are catching a train, it is always better to be comfortably early than even a fraction of a minute too late.
words.zh: 如果您要赶火车，早到总是比迟到一分钟要好。

words.en: Although being early may mean wasting a little time, this will be less than if you miss the train and have to wait an hour or more for the next one; and you avoid the frustration of arriving at the very moment when the train is drawing out of the station and being unable to get on it.
words.zh: 虽然早到可能会浪费一点时间，但这比错过火车而要等下一趟火车一个小时或更长时间要少；而且您还可以避免在火车即将出站时到达却无法上车的沮丧。

words.en: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.
words.zh: 更困难的情况是，在火车准时到达站台时，却仍然眼睁睁地看着火车在没有你的情况下开走。

words.en: Such an experience befell a certain young girl the first time she was travelling alone.
words.zh: 某位年轻女孩第一次独自旅行时，就遇到了这样的经历。

words.en: She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due, since her parents had impressed upon her that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
words.zh: 她在火车到站时间前二十分钟进了车站，因为她的父母告诉她，错过火车将是不可原谅的，并且会导致她留下来的朋友们长途跋涉两趟来接她。

words.en: She gave her luggage to a porter and showed him her ticket.
words.zh: 她把行李交给搬运工，并向他出示了车票。

words.en: To her horror he said that she was two hours too soon.
words.zh: 令她惊恐的是，他说她来得太早了两个小时。

words.en: She felt in her handbag for the piece of paper on which her father had written down all the details of the journey and gave it to the porter.
words.zh: 她在手提包里摸索着一张纸，她父亲在上面写下了旅程的所有细节，然后把它交给了搬运工。

words.en: He agreed that a train did come into the station at the time on the paper and that it did stop, but only to take on mail, not passengers.
words.zh: 他同意报纸上当时确实有一列火车进站并且确实停下来，但只是为了运送邮件，而不是乘客。

words.en: The girl asked to see a timetable, feeling sure that her father could not have made such a mistake.
words.zh: 女孩要求看一下时刻表，她确信父亲不会犯这样的错误。

words.en: The porter went to fetch one and arrived back with the station master, who produced it with a flourish and pointed out a microscopic 'o' beside the time of the arrival of the train at his station; this little 'o' indicated that the train only stopped for mail.
words.zh: 搬运工去拿了一张，然后和站长一起回来了，站长把它拿出来，并指着火车到站时间旁边的一个微小的“o”；这个小“o”表示火车只是为了邮寄邮件而停下来。

words.en: Just as that moment the train came into the station.
words.zh: 就在这时，火车进站了。

words.en: The girl, tears streaming down her face, begged to be allowed to slip into the guard's van.
words.zh: 女孩泪流满面，请求允许进入警卫的货车。

words.en: But the station master was adamant: rules could not be broken.
words.zh: 但站长态度坚决：规则不能违反。

words.en: And she had to watch that train disappear towards her destination while she was left behind.
words.zh: 她只能眼睁睁地看着火车驶向目的地，而她却被抛在后面。
